### Can I see a doctor, physiotherapist or chiropractor while I'm on my overseas trip?

If you are unexpectedly sick or injured while overseas, your Fast Cover Travel Insurance policy may provide cover for your medical expenses under the medical expenses related benefits Depending on the expenses that you are claiming for, the medical expenses and related benefits can reimburse you for the reasonable costs of medical treatment you receive while overseas if you become unexpectedly sick or injured, which can include consultations with a doctor, physiotherapist, or chiropractor. Cover is subject to the terms, conditions, exclusions, and limits outlined in the Product Disclosure Statement (PDS).

If you become unexpectedly sick or injured while overseas, you may see a doctor for consultation and treatment. Generally, you will need to pay for the consultation upfront and submit a claim for reimbursement with the necessary supporting documents, including receipts and a detailed medical report for your claim to be reviewed.

If you are unexpectedly injured and require physiotherapy or chiropractic care, you can claim for up to two weeks of treatment. The treatment must be related to a claimable event as listed in the Product Disclosure Statement and confirmed in writing by a medical practitioner. If you need more than two weeks of treatment, you must contact our Emergency Assistance team for approval.

Please note that there are specific situations where medical expenses may not be covered under your policy. It is important that you read the relevant PDS and are aware of the terms and conditions, exclusions, limit and sub limits that may apply. Some examples of situations that are not covered under our policies include but are not limited to:

- Routine medical, dental, physiotherapy, or chiropractic check-ups, even if your medical condition is approved for cover by us following a medical screening
- Elective medical, dental, or cosmetic surgery or for any complications or other claims arising from such procedures or treatments. Even if your medical condition is approved for cover by us following a medical screening. Whether performed overseas or in Australia. This means that if you have elective medical or dental or cosmetic surgery, you would not be able to claim for any medical, cancellation or trip disruption expenses if you experience any direct or indirect complications from the surgery.
- Any medical expenses incurred in Australia
- Medical expenses once you return to Australia, even if the medical issue occurred overseas and we have approved your medical repatriation back to Australia

Eligibility criteria, policy terms, conditions, exclusions, limits and sub limits apply. Consider the PDS prior to deciding on which policy is right for you and your needs.

Any advice is general advice only and does not take into account your individual objectives, financial situation, or needs. Please consider the PDS before making any decisions regarding the purchase of travel insurance.

As each individual’s circumstances are different, we will assess each claim on a case-by-case basis in accordance with your specific circumstances, policy terms, and Certificate of Insurance.

### Can I ride a motorcycle overseas with a licence issued by Motorcycling Australia?

Fast Cover Travel insurance does not automatically cover you for riding a motorcycle overseas with a license issued by Motorcycling Australia. If you plan to ride or be a passenger on a motorcycle, moped, or scooter while overseas, you can purchase the Motorcycle Pack as an add-on to your Fast Cover travel insurance policy, provided you are eligible, please refer to the eligibility criteria for Motorcycle Pack in the Product Disclosure Statement (PDS).

Motorcycle Pack add-on is available under our Frequent Traveller Saver policy, Snow Sports policy, Comprehensive policy, Standard Saver policy, and Basic policy. Please note that Motorcycle Pack is not available under our domestic policy.

You must meet the specific licensing requirements for the type of vehicle you intend to ride. If You are the rider in control of a motorcycle, moped or scooter with an engine capacity of 125cc or less, you must hold both a current Australian Drivers Licence (Provisional or higher) (regardless of the local laws) and a licence valid for the country that You are riding in.

If You are the rider in control of a motorcycle, moped or scooter with an engine capacity greater than 125cc, you must hold both a current Australian Motorcycle Licence (Provisional or higher) valid for the same class of motorcycle, moped or scooter (regardless of the local laws) and a licence valid for the country that You are riding in.

Cover under the Motorcycle Pack benefit is subject to the terms, conditions, exclusions, limits, and sub-limits outlined in the Product Disclosure Statement (PDS). It is important that you carefully read and understand these terms to ensure the cover is suitable for your needs. Coverage is only available if eligibility criteria are met, and it is your responsibility to comply with the licensing requirements of the country you are travelling to.

Eligibility criteria, policy terms, conditions, exclusions, limits and sub limits apply. Consider the PDS prior to deciding on which policy is right for you and your needs.

### Can travel insurance cover me if I fall victim to a scam?

### Can you get a Bali visa online?

### Can you fly pregnant at 8 months?

High altitudes and long-haul flights can increase risks of blood clots. If you must fly, consult your doctor, confirm with your airline, and wear compression stockings to reduce the risk of blood clots. Safety for both you and your baby should come first.

### Do children need to be insured on a travel insurance policy?

Children need to be listed on a policy if you want them to have cover while travelling. A child can be included under a Family policy, a Single policy with a parent, or they can hold their own separate policy.

To be considered as a dependant on your policy, children must be aged 20 years and under , not in full-time employment, and travelling with at least one of the adults named on the Certificate of Insurance for the full itinerary.

If a cild is not insured under a policy, they will not have travel insurance cover for the trip.

### Can siblings and their children be covered together under a Family travel insurance policy?

A Family policy has a specific definition and does not extend to siblings travelling together with their children. Family policies can only cover:

- You, your spouse (or someone legally recognised in Australia as your de facto partner) and your dependant children; or
- You, your spouse/partner and your grandchildren; or
- You, your son or daughter and your grandchildren.

To be included as a Dependant, children or grandchildren must be aged 20 and under and not in full-time employment.

If you are travelling with a sister and her child, each traveller would need to purchase their own separate policy to ensure everyone is covered.

### Do I have a medical condition for travel insurance purposes?

A Medical Condition means any bodily or physical injury, physical defect, illness, disease or other medical or dental Condition or sign or symptom of these things, the applicable person:

- required prescription medication for or has been prescribed medication from a medical practitioner in writing for,
- sought or received medical advice from a medical practitioner or other health care professional for,
- had tests, investigations, care, treatment or medical attention including surgery for,
- been admitted to hospital for (including emergency department or day surgery procedure), or
- became aware of or which a reasonable person in the circumstances would have been aware of.

It includes but is not limited to:

- the suffering or treatment of mental illness,
- a brain, heart (such as any cardiovascular or coronary heart disease or any condition related to a heart or blood vessels), kidney, liver, respiratory, circulatory (such as high blood pressure, stroke, or transient ischaemic attack), cancer or cancerous condition,
- reduced or deficient immune system,
- a sign or symptom of the above matters, or
- an allergy or food intolerance,
- a persistent and lasting condition in medicine such as constant pain or long-suffering pain or pain with a pattern of relapse and remission.
- any conditions related to previous and current pregnancy as detailed in What is a Pregnancy Condition and in the ‘Pregnancy Cover’ section of the Product Disclosure Statement (PDS).

Every claim is reviewed individually on a case-by-case basis and will only be paid if it meets the terms, conditions, limits, and exclusions in your policy. Always check the PDS carefully so you know exactly what’s included before you travel.

*Source: <https://fastcover.com.au/faq/do-i-have-a-medical-condition-for-travel-insurance-purposes>*

### Do Australians need a Schengen visa?

Australian citizens and residents with passport nationality form an [ETIAS eligible country](https://www.etiaseu.eu/etias-eligible-countries/) do not need a Schengen visa for short stays of up to 90 days within any 180-day period when travelling for tourism, business, or family visits.

However, Australian residents with passport nationality from a country that is not eligible for ETIAS must apply for a Schengen visa for short stays of up to 90 days within any 180-day period when travelling for tourism, business, or family visits.

Generally, all Australians intending to stay in Europe beyond these permitted short-term stay periods, or for purposes such as work or study will need to apply for a national visa (Type D) from the specific country where they plan to stay.

As entry and visa requirements for Europe and the Schengen Area may change over time, it is your responsibility to verify entry and visa requirements with the official government authorities including the [European Commission](https://home-affairs.ec.europa.eu/policies/schengen/visa-policy) and the embassy or consulate of the European country you plan to visit.

### Do I need a motorbike licence if I am riding a quad bike?

You do not need a motorcycle licence if you are riding a quad bike.

However, you are not automatically covered for quad bike riding and recreational all-terrain vehicles.

Cover is available to ride a quad bike or recreational ATV, if you:

- Take out the [Adventure Pack](https://fastcover.com.au/adventure-travel-insurance) and pay the additional premium,
- Ride the quad bike or ATV under the direct supervision of a properly licensed recreational organisation,
- Obey all relevant safety codes,
- Wear protective gloves and a crash helmet suitable for the activity
- Were a single rider with maximum one passenger, and
- Do not engage in jumping, racing or competition while riding the quad bike or ATV.

Note the Adventure Pack is not available with the Basics policy.

As each individual’s circumstances are different, we will assess each claim on a case-by-case basis and in accordance with your specific circumstances, relevant policy terms and conditions, and Certificate of Insurance.

### Do I need a return ticket for my policy to be valid?

If you’re an **Australian citizen or permanent resident**, you don’t need to hold a return ticket for your policy to be valid, but your trip must end in Australia. When buying your policy, you can simply enter the date you plan to return home as your “Return Date.” This sets the length of your cover. Policies can be extended online while overseas, but they cannot be shortened once issued.

If you’re a temporary resident of Australia, for example, **non-Australian citizen or non-permanent resident**, you must hold a valid return ticket to Australia at the time of purchase. This is one of the eligibility requirements for purchasing a Fast Cover travel insurance policy.

Every claim is reviewed individually on a case-by-case basis and will only be paid if it meets the terms, conditions, limits, and exclusions in your policy. Always check the PDS carefully so you know exactly what’s included before you travel.

*Source: <https://fastcover.com.au/faq/do-i-need-a-return-ticket-for-my-policy-to-be-valid>*

### Do cruises require special travel insurance?

Travel insurance for cruising is different to a holiday where you're flying, taking the train or bus to your destination, simply because you're on the sea or ocean! If a serious emergency occurs, the ship's medical facilities may not be equipped to treat you adequately, and you may need to be evacuated off the ship and taken to a hospital on land.

That's why it is important to consider travel insurance for cruising. And that's also why a cruise travel insurance policy may cost a little more, as it provides you with certain cover for evacuation off the ship to an overseas hospital, or repatriation back to Australia for treatment.

Eligibility criteria, policy terms, conditions, exclusions and limits apply. Consider the PDS prior to deciding on which policy is right for you and your needs.

*Source: <https://fastcover.com.au/faq/do-cruises-require-special-travel-insurance>*

### Do I Need a Visa for Malaysia from Australia?

Currently Australian citizens do not need a visa for Malaysia from Australia for short visits. You can stay visa-free for up to 90 days under Malaysia's visa exemption program. However, if you plan to stay longer or visit for other purposes like work or study, you will need to apply for the appropriate entry permit before travelling to Malaysia.

*Source: <https://fastcover.com.au/faq/do-i-need-a-visa-for-malaysia-from-australia>*

### Do Australians need to submit an e-Arrival Card to enter South Korea?

Yes, Australian travellers need to submit the [Korean Electronic Arrival Card](https://www.e-arrivalcard.go.kr/portal/main/index.do) known as the e-Arrival Card before they enter South Korea. This electronic system allows travellers to conveniently submit their arrival declaration form online. Online application is available starting 3 days before arrival in South Korea and is free. Applicants can submit individual or group arrival cards.

As entry and visa requirements for South Korea may change, it is your responsibility to verify entry and visa requirements with official government sources such as the [South Korean Embassy](https://southkorea.embassy.gov.au/) in Australia or your local South Korean Consulate.

*Source: <https://fastcover.com.au/faq/do-australians-need-to-submit-an-e-arrival-card-to-enter-south-korea>*

### Do I Need a Visa for New Zealand from Australia?

Australian citizens travelling on an Australian passport, and Australian permanent residents travelling with a valid and per-approved New Zealand Electronic Travel Authority do not need to apply for a visa to enter New Zealand as they will be granted an Australian Resident Visa upon arrival, allowing you to visit, work, study, and live in New Zealand indefinitely, provided they meet all the entry requirements.

However, Australian temporary residents may need a visa for New Zealand, depending on their passport nationality, purpose and duration of their trip. Australian temporary residents should use New Zealand Immigration’s [online tool to check if they need a visa or an NZeTA](https://www.immigration.govt.nz/visit/what-you-need-to-visit-new-zealand/check-if-you-need-a-visa-or-an-nzeta/) to travel to New Zealand based on their specific circumstances.

Any advice is general advice only and does not take into account your individual objectives, financial situation, or needs. As entry requirements for New Zealand may change over time, it is your responsibility to verify entry and visa requirements with the official government authorities including [**Immigration New Zealand**](https://www.immigration.govt.nz/), [**New Zealand Customs Service**](https://www.customs.govt.nz/), the New Zealand High Commission, the New Zealand Consulate General, and the [**Australian Department of Home Affairs**](https://www.homeaffairs.gov.au/).

*Source: <https://fastcover.com.au/faq/do-i-need-a-visa-for-new-zealand-from-australia>*

### Do I need a visa for travelling to the UK?

Australian citizens travelling to the UK for less than six months as a tourist usually won’t need a visa. Australian tourists now require an [**Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA)**](https://www.visitbritain.com/en/plan-your-trip/visa-and-immigration-information) to visit Britain (England, Scotland, and Wales) and Northern Ireland, for visits up to six months. Generally, you can visit the UK as a Standard Visitor for tourism, business, study (courses up to 6 months) and other permitted activities for a period of up to 6 months.

You may need a visa to enter the UK to visit, study or work, depending on the nature and duration of your trip. As visa and entry requirements for the UK may change over time, it is your responsibility to verify visa requirements from a UK embassy or consulate or the UK government website. To [**check if you need a UK visa**](https://www.gov.uk/check-uk-visa), visit the UK Government website.

For more information about Australian’s visa requirements for European travel, including the UK, read our guide on [**Europe visa requirements**](../blog/visa-requirements/europe-and-schengen-visa-requirements).

*Source: <https://fastcover.com.au/faq/do-i-need-a-visa-for-travelling-to-the-uk>*

### Do I need a visa for travelling to Vietnam?

All Australia citizens must have a valid visa or visa exemption certificate to enter Vietnam.

As visa and entry requirements for Vietnam may change over time, it is your responsibility to verify visa requirements from the [**Vietnamese embassy website**](https://vietnamembassy.org.au/en/visa-viet-nam), your local [**Vietnam embassy or consulate**,](https://protocol.dfat.gov.au/Public/Missions/217) or from the [**Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Vietnam visa application website**](https://visa.mofa.gov.vn/Homepage.aspx).

### Do I have to pay anything if I make a claim?

If an excess applies to the particular benefit you are claiming under, you will need to pay or bear the excess if you make a claim. This means that any payable excess will need to be deducted from your settlement or you will need to pay the excess amount when you make a claim, therefore reducing the amount of your claim.

For policies purchased BEFORE you have departed Australia, the excess on claims depends on the excess you chose at the time that you purchased your policy. It may also depend on the benefit you make a claim under.

For policies purchased AFTER you have already left Australia (already overseas policies), the excess is $500. It is NOT possible to reduce or remove this excess.

Cover is subject to the policy terms, conditions, limits and exclusions in the [Product Disclosure Statement (PDS)](https://fastcover.com.au/pds).

#### Related Articles

- What is an Excess?

*Source: <https://fastcover.com.au/faq/do-i-have-to-pay-anything-if-i-make-a-claim>*

### Do I need an electronic travel authorization to travel to Canada?

Visa-exempt Australians travelling to Canada by air must have an Electronic Travel Authorization (eTA), even if only transiting through a Canadian airport. The eTA is valid for up to five years and allows multiple entries. It's not required for entry by land or sea.

Any advice is general advice only and does not take into account your individual objectives, financial situation, or needs. As entry and visa requirements for Canada may change over time, it is your responsibility to verify entry and visa requirements with the official government authorities including the [Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship.html), the [Canada Border Services Agency](https://www.cbsa-asfc.gc.ca/), and the [Canadian High Commission in Australia](https://www.international.gc.ca/country-pays/australia-australie/index.aspx?lang=eng).

### Do I have to pay the bill for medical claims and then claim them back when I return home?

If you receive medical treatment overseas, you’ll generally need to pay the bill upfront, keep the receipt, and obtain a medical certificate that details your illness, injury, or sickness and the treatment provided. You can then submit a claim when you return home.

If you are hospitalised, you or someone in your travelling party must contact the Fast Cover Emergency Assistance team as soon as possible. They are available 24/7 and can:

- Help with medical problems and liaise with treating doctors,
- Locate the nearest appropriate medical facilities,
- Arrange repatriation to Australia if medically necessary,
- Keep your loved ones or workplace informed if needed.

If you do not contact Emergency Assistance when it is reasonably possible to do so, we may not pay for these expenses or for any evacuation or flights that were not approved or arranged by us (to the extent permitted by law).

If you are not hospitalised, but your outpatient treatment costs are expected to exceed $2,000, you must also contact Emergency Assistance as soon as possible. Even if the costs are less, you can still contact them anytime for support.

Please note: If you submit a claim, an **excess** may apply to each claimable event. This will be deducted from the total claim amount, reducing the final amount paid.

**Emergency Assistance contact details:**

- From Australia: **02 8320 7999**
- From overseas: **+61 2 8320 7999**
- Email: [emergency@fastcover.com.au](mailto:emergency@fastcover.com.au)

*Source: <https://fastcover.com.au/faq/do-i-have-to-pay-the-bill-for-medical-claims-and-then-claim-them-back-when-i-return-home>*

### Do I need a visa for Bali from Australia?

Australians need a visa for travelling to Bali. However, the type of visa and when you apply for it may vary depending on the purpose of your trip and the length of your stay. Australians travelling to Bali for tourism, official government duties or business purposes can apply for a visa on arrival once they arrive in Bali. Australians can also apply for an electronic visa on arrival (e-VOA) through the [Directorate General of Immigration e-Visa website](https://evisa.imigrasi.go.id/) or through the [All Indonesia Arrival Card website](https://allindonesia.imigrasi.go.id/), at least 48 hours before travelling to Indonesia. If you do not apply for an e-VOA at least 48 hours in advance of your travel to Indonesia, you can still apply for a regular Visa on Arrival (VOA) at certain international airports, seaports and land crossings, including Jakarta, Bali, Surabaya, Makassar, Lombok, Batam, Medan, Manado, Aceh, Padang, Tanjung Pinang and Yogyakarta. You cannot transit in Indonesia without an e-VOA or VOA.

For longer stays or other purposes like work, or study, you'll need to obtain the appropriate visa before travelling to Bali, Indonesia.

Any advice is general advice only and does not take into account your individual objectives, financial situation, or needs. Please do not consider any information contained in this document as visa advice, or complete or most current information. As entry and visa requirements for Bali may change over time, it is your responsibility to verify entry and visa requirements with the official government authorities including the [Indonesian Directorate General of Immigration](https://www.imigrasi.go.id/), the [Indonesian Embassy in Australia](https://kemlu.go.id/canberra/en), or your local Indonesian Consulate.

*Source: <https://fastcover.com.au/faq/do-i-need-a-visa-for-bali-from-australia>*

### Do I Need a Visa for Europe from Australia?

Australian citizens and residents with passport nationality from an [ETIAS eligible country](https://www.etiaseu.eu/etias-eligible-countries/) do not need a visa to enter the 29 countries in the Schengen Area within Europe for short-term visits of up to 90 days in a 180-day period for tourism or business purposes. The 29 countries in the Schengen Area include Austria, Belgium, Croatia, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Iceland, Italy, Latvia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Romania and Bulgaria. From late 2026, visa-exempt Australians will need to apply for [European Travel Information and Authorisation System (ETIAS)](https://home-affairs.ec.europa.eu/policies/schengen/smart-borders/european-travel-information-authorisation-system_en) approval before travelling to the Schengen Area

Australian residents with passport nationality from non-eligible ETIAS countries must apply for the Schengen Visa for short-term visits of up to 90 days in a 180-day period for tourism or business purposes.

Several non-Schengen Area countries in Europe also offer visa-free travel to Australian passport holders travelling for tourism. Countries including Albania, Armenia, Belarus, Bosnia & Herzegovina, Cyprus, Georgia, Ireland, Kosovo, Moldova, Montenegro, Republic of North Macedonia, Serbia and the United Kingdom provide visa-free travel for tourism stays typically for up to at least 90 days.

Australians intending to travel to Europe for longer stays beyond the visa-free travel period or beyond the short-stay period permitted by the Schengen visa, or for purposes such as work or study will need to apply for the appropriate national visa from the embassy or consulate of the European country where they intend to stay.

As entry and visa requirements for Europe and the Schengen Area may change over time, it is your responsibility to verify entry and visa requirements with the official government authorities including the [European Commission](https://home-affairs.ec.europa.eu/policies/schengen/visa-policy) and the embassy or consulate of the European country you plan to visit.

*Source: <https://fastcover.com.au/faq/do-i-need-a-visa-for-europe-from-australia>*

### Do I need a visa for the UK from Australia?

From the 25th of February 2026, travellers who successfully apply for a visa to the UK will be issued with an eVisa. Keep in mind, you may not need an eVisa (or visa generally) if you are visiting the UK with an electronic travel authorisation (ETA), or if you are a dual citizen required to use your British or Irish passport to enter the UK.

From the 25th of February 2026, Australian-British or Australian-Irish dual citizens must enter the UK on their British or Irish passport, or through a certificate of entitlement in another valid passport. These dual citizens cannot enter the UK with an ETA or other visa.

### Do I need family travel insurance?

Your family travel insurance can cover you for the unexpected costs of your family holiday, including [overseas medical expenses](../travel-insurance-guide/overseas-emergency-medical-and-hospital-expenses), [rental vehicle insurance excess](../rental-vehicle-insurance-excess-cover), cancellations due to illness or injury and the replacement of [lost or stolen belongings](../travel-insurance-guide/travel-insurance-for-luggage-and-personal-effects).

For more information, refer to our [Product Disclosure Statement (PDS)](https://fastcover.com.au/pds).

### Do I need to do a medical screening for pregnancy when buying travel insurance?

Pregnancy itself is not automatically treated as a condition that generally requires a medical screening, as long as the pregnancy is progressing normally and falls within the gestational limits outlined in the policy.

A medical screening may be required if you have pregnancy related complications, an existing medical condition, or if a medical professional has advised that your pregnancy is high risk. In these situations, you can complete a medical screening to check whether cover may be available for the specific medical or pregnancy related condition. If cover is offered, an additional premium may apply, depending on the condition being assessed.

Every claim is reviewed individually on a case-by-case basis and will only be paid if it meets the terms, conditions, limits, and exclusions in your policy. Always check the PDS carefully so you know exactly what’s included before you travel.

*Source: <https://fastcover.com.au/faq/do-i-need-to-do-a-medical-screening-for-pregnancy-when-buying-travel-insurance>*

### Do I need to register for eTravel if I go to the Philippines?

Yes, all foreign travellers including Australians need to register their travel to the Philippines online with eTravel, within 72 hours or 3 days of their scheduled arrival date. Keep in mind that this does not replace a visa. If you intend on staying in the Philippines beyond the 30 day visa-free period for Australians, you will need to obtain the relevant visa for your trip.

As entry and visa requirements for the Philippines may change over time, it is your responsibility to verify entry and visa requirements with official government sources such as the [Philippine Department of Foreign Affairs](https://dfa.gov.ph/), [Philippine Embassy](https://philembassy.org.au/consular/visa) or the [Consulate General](https://sydneypcg.dfa.gov.ph/79-consular-services/705-general-information-on-visas).

*Source: <https://fastcover.com.au/faq/do-i-need-to-register-for-etravel-if-i-go-to-the-philippines>*

### Do I need to do a medical screening?

You may need to do a medical screening if you’d like cover for an existing medical condition or a pregnancy-related condition.

We agree to list the relevant medical condition or pregnancy condition as covered on your Certificate of insurance. If any changes in health occur after we have listed any medical condition or pregnancy condition as covered and before the date of departure for your trip, the cover for those listed conditions are automatically excluded from the time the changes in health occurred, unless you undertake an additional medical screening and we agree to list them as covered.

Any cover is subject to the other terms and conditions (including exclusions and limits) of the policy which may otherwise affect cover. Any rights we have will only be exercised to the extent permitted by applicable law.

See General Exclusions that apply to all benefits in PDS. After the date of departure for your trip, We will not agree to list a medical condition as covered on your Certificate of insurance. No cover is provided under this policy for any claims arising from, or any way related to a medical condition or pregnancy condition which existed within the period of 3 years prior to the policy issue date, of any person who is not named on your Certificate of insurance, except as specifically considered as close relative conditions under Benefit 5: Trip Cancellation Expenses, Benefit 6: Trip Disruption Expenses or Benefit 7: Trip Resumption Expenses.

If you’re unsure whether you need to complete a medical screening, you can always reach out to our friendly Customer Service team on 1300 409 322 or email info@fastcover.com.au. They’ll be more than happy to help you figure it out.

Every claim is reviewed individually on a case-by-case basis and will only be paid if it meets the terms, conditions, limits, and exclusions in your policy. Always check the PDS carefully so you know exactly what’s included before you travel.

### Do I need to tell you the amount of the input tax credit for my policy?

### Do I need to add on the Adventure pack for doing the rock wall climbing on the ship?

Outdoor rock wall climbing on a cruise is included as a listed activity under the Adventure Pack. This means you’ll need to purchase the Adventure Pack add-on with your Fast Cover travel insurance policy for the activity to be considered under your cover. It must be done only with a licensed commercial operator using ropes and appropriate safety gear. Free solo climbing is not covered.

Indoor rock climbing on a cruise is included within the Covered Sports and Leisure Activities under Fast Cover travel insurance policies. This activity must be carried out under appropriate supervision.

All climbing activities must be undertaken recreationally and not in a professional or competitive capacity. The Adventure Pack is not available with the Basics policy.

### Do I need to upgrade my travel insurance to a higher region if I’m only stopping over for less than 48 hours?

If your stopover in a destination that is not listed on your policy or not included in the region listed on your policy, is less than 48 hours and you do not leave the airport, you do not need to make changes to the policy. However, if the stopover is within 48 hours but you leave the airport then the country will need to be listed.

This means you would only need to update the destinations or region on your policy if you plan to stay in that higher region for more than 48 hours or if you leave the airport during your stopover.

Every claim is reviewed individually on a case-by-case basis and will only be paid if it meets the terms, conditions, limits, and exclusions in your policy. Always check the PDS carefully so you know exactly what’s included before you travel.

### Do I still need to apply for a visa if I have the Thailand Digital Arrival Card?

The Thailand Digital Arrival Card (TDAC) will not change Thailand’s visa requirements. Therefore, if you require a visa to enter Thailand, you must still apply for the relevant visa and obtain the TDAC before your arrival to Thailand. For visa-exempt travellers, the TDAC will function as a pre-arrival registration system, similar to Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) documents in other countries.

### Do receipts, medical or police reports have to be translated into English for my claim?

When you initially submit your claim to Fast Cover, you should attach your original, untranslated documentation for the Claims team to review. This includes any receipts, medical reports, police reports, or other supporting documents directly related to your claim. The claims team will assess your claim based on the information provided.

If the claims team determines that your documentation needs to be translated, they will contact you to request for translation. Translation fees are not covered by your travel insurance policy.

You have two options for translation:

- You can choose to pay for the translation through an external company selected by Fast Cover, or
- You may use your own translation service, provided that the translation is completed by a translator accredited by the National Accreditation Authority for Translators and Interpreters (NAATI).

Eligibility criteria, policy terms, conditions, exclusions, limits and sub limits apply. Consider the PDS prior to deciding on which policy is right for you and your needs.

Any advice is general advice only and does not take into account your individual objectives, financial situation, or needs. Please consider the PDS before making any decisions regarding the purchase of travel insurance.

### Does domestic travel insurance provide any medical cover if I'm travelling in Australia?

Fast Cover’s Domestic Plus travel insurance policy does not provide cover for medical emergencies and medical expenses incurred whilst you are travelling in Australia because medical expenses are covered by Medicare and/or your private health insurance.

In the event of a medical emergency while you are travelling domestically, you should call 000 for assistance as you would normally do if you were at home. You can also seek assistance from the relevant authorities where you are visiting, including the resort, hotel, airline, bus line or train line.

If you are travelling within Australia and you have an existing medical condition, you can compete a medical screening to apply to include cover for your existing medical condition under applicable policy benefits such as trip cancellation cover. ### Does Japan have a visa exemption for Australians?

Yes, under Japan’s Visa Exemption Scheme, Australians visiting Japan for short-term travel, such as tourism, business, and visiting family or friends do not need to apply for a tourist visa. This exemption permits stays of up to 90 days, provided travellers do not engage in paid or unpaid work. However, if your trip requires a longer stay or involves activities like study or work in Japan, you will need to apply for a visa.

Entry requirements for Japan may change over time, so make sure to verify visa requirements with the [Japanese Embassy in Australia](https://www.au.emb-japan.go.jp/), your local Japanese consulate or the [Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan](https://www.mofa.go.jp/).

### Does the Loss of Income benefit cover sickness?

No, the **Loss of Income** benefit only applies if you are unable to work to return to your usual occupation in Australia because of an injury caused by an accident during your overseas trip or as mentioned in your policy. It does not provide cover if you are unable to work due to sickness or illness.

We will pay if you are Injured during your overseas trip and become disabled within 30 days of the injury date because of the injury, and the disablement continues for more than 30 days after your return from your overseas trip to your home (your “waiting period”), and you are unable to return to your usual occupation in Australia,

### Does Fast Cover travel insurance cover natural disasters?

Fast Cover travel insurance can cover natural disaster related events, but it depends on when the event occurs and how it affects your trip.

If the natural disaster was known, forecast, or already impacting your destination before you purchased your policy, related claims are generally not covered. ### Does the unlimited cancellation benefit apply to the first trip on a Frequent Traveller Saver policy?

The **c**ancellation benefit on a Frequent Traveller Saver policy begins on the start date you choose when you set up your policy. This means it’s up to you whether cover begins straight away or only from the day you leave on your first trip.

Here’s how it works:

- **If you choose your purchase date as the start date of Trip Cancellation Benefit**

Your cancellation cover begins immediately. For example, if you buy your policy four weeks before your trip and select the purchase date as the start date, you’ll have cancellation cover during those four weeks. If something unexpected happens (like an injury) and you can’t travel, you can submit a claim for cancellation costs (subject to policy terms and conditions).
- **If you choose your departure date as the start date of Trip Cancellation Benefit**

Your cancellation cover only begins on the day you leave. Using the same example, if you get injured two weeks before your trip but you selected your departure date as the start date, there would be no cancellation cover in place for that time.

So, cancellation cover does apply to your first trip, but it only starts from the date you’ve nominated on your Certificate of Insurance.

Every claim is reviewed individually on a case-by-case basis and will only be paid if it meets the terms, conditions, limits, and exclusions in your policy. Always check the PDS carefully so you know exactly what’s included before you travel.

*Source: <https://fastcover.com.au/faq/does-the-unlimited-cancellation-benefit-apply-to-the-first-trip-on-a-frequent-traveller-saver-policy>*

### Does the US have a visa exemption for Australians?

Yes, the United States includes Australia in the [Visa Waiver Program](https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/us-visas/tourism-visit/visa-waiver-program.html). Under the Visa Waiver Program, Australians staying in the US for less than 90 days for tourism or business purposes won't need to apply for a visa before entering the United States, provided they have [a valid ESTA authorisation](https://esta.cbp.dhs.gov/).

Any advice is general advice only and does not take into account your individual objectives, financial situation, or needs. As entry and visa requirements for the US may change over time, it is your responsibility to verify entry and visa requirements with the official government authorities including the [US Department of State - Bureau of Consular Affairs](https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/us-visas.html), the [United States Customs and Border Protection](https://www.cbp.gov/) (CBP), the [US Embassy in Australia](https://au.usembassy.gov/visas/) or your local US Consulate.

### Does travel insurance cover flight changes?

Depending on the reason for the flight changes and the policy chosen, and depending on the type of expenses you are seeking, cover may be available under the policy benefits for flight changes. Some of the benefits that might be relevant, include but are not limited to:

The Trip Cancellation Expenses benefit can reimburse you for costs such as your non-refundable pre-paid trip bookings which can include flights, for reasons covered under the policy.

Trip Disruption Expenses benefit is available to provide protection against the financial burden of reasonable additional costs which can include flight changes, you incur whilst you are still on your trip, if it is interrupted for reasons covered under the policy benefit.

Our Travel Delay Expenses benefit can reimburse you up to $200 for each traveller (excluding Dependants) for the reasonable additional meals and accommodation expenses during your trip, if your flight has been cancelled, rescheduled or delayed for at least 6 hours from the time it was scheduled to depart.

#### What are some of the types of situations flight changes may be covered?

Below are just some examples of some situations in which flight changes may be covered under your policy. It is important to read the PDS prior to deciding which policy is right for you and your particular trip, and relevant terms, conditions, exclusions, limits and sub-limits that apply:

- If the flight was cancelled due to a reason that is covered under the policy, such as an unexpected illness or injury that prevents you from travelling.
- If your scheduled or connecting flight is cancelled, delayed, shortened or diverted due to a natural disaster.

#### What are some of the situations that flight changes may not be covered?

These are a few examples of some situations in which flight changes may not be covered. It is important that you read the relevant PDS and are aware of the terms and conditions, exclusions, limits and sub limits that may apply:

- Where you or your travel companion change plans or decide not to continue with the intended trip.
- Failure to comply with ticketing or booking conditions or requirements, such as missing your flight due to arriving late for reasons within your control.

Eligibility criteria, policy terms, conditions, exclusions, limits and sub limits apply. Consider the PDS prior to deciding on which policy is right for you and your needs.

Any advice is general advice only and does not take into account your individual objectives, financial situation, or needs. Please consider the PDS before making any decisions regarding the purchase of travel insurance.

As each individual’s circumstances are different, we will assess each claim on a case-by-case basis in accordance with your specific circumstances, policy terms, and Certificate of Insurance.

### Does travel insurance cover carrier operational issues like staffing shortages or mechanical problems?

Most travel insurance policies do not provide cover for carrier operational issues such as staffing shortages, technical, or mechanical problems simply because they occurred. Instead, cover may apply under certain policy benefits for reasonable additional expenses you incur as a result of the carrier's operational issues.

For example, depending on the policy you choose at Fast Cover Travel Insurance, cover may be available under the following benefits subject to the policy terms and conditions:

**Travel Delay Expenses:**Up to $200 per insured adult, per day, for reasonable additional accommodation and meal costs if your carrier is delayed for more than 6 hours and for each subsequent 24-hour period beyond the initial 6-hour delay. The total benefit limit is up to $2,000.

**Special Event Transport Expenses:** Up to $5,000 for reasonable additional travel expenses to reach the special event on time if your scheduled transport is cancelled, delayed, shortened or diverted during your trip and that means you would not arrive on time.

**Important to know:**

- These benefits are only available on select policies.
- Special events means pre-booked, pre-paid and pre-arranged wedding, funeral, conference, concert, sporting event, cruise or tour package.
- There is no cover for Trip Cancellation Expenses or Trip Disruption Expenses if your carrier reschedules or cancels your scheduled or connecting transport, unless it’s due to a strike, riot, hijack, civil protest, severe weather, or natural disaster.

Every claim is reviewed individually on a case-by-case basis and will only be paid if it meets the terms, conditions, limits, and exclusions in your policy. Always check the PDS carefully so you know exactly what’s included before you travel.

### Does travel insurance cover cruises?

Cover for travelling on cruise ship is available provided you specify this at the time you purchase your policy. However, cover for travelling on a cruise ship is automatically included with the Frequent Traveller Saver Policy.

For an overseas trip, you must select cruise cover for your policy to include cover for claims related to travel on a cruise ship or arising whilst on a cruise ship.

For a domestic trip, you must select cruise cover for pour policy to include cover for claims related to travel on a cruise ship or arising whilst on a cruise ship. If you are travelling on a cruise ship within Australian waters (including a remote area within Australia, but not a remote area on land within Australia), your cover is extended to allow for you to be evacuated to a location where Australian emergency services can pick you up and transfer you to an Australian medical facility for treatment if you are Injured or become Sick. Your cover is also extended for certain medical expenses incurred whilst on-board the cruise ship if you are Injured or become Sick. We will not pay for any medical expenses or medical transportation which is provided on land in Australia.

If travelling on a Cruise ship:

• Within Australian waters, the New Zealand or the South Pacific Region for 1 night or more you must specify cruise cover at time of purchase.

• Within Asia, Europe or Worldwide Regions for 4 nights or more you must specify cruise cover at time of purchase.

• On a river cruise: You do not need cruise cover.

*Source: <https://fastcover.com.au/faq/does-travel-insurance-cover-international-transaction-fees-if-i-cancel-my-trip>*

### Does travel insurance cover me for my medical expenses if I drive a friend's car when I'm overseas?

Depending on the policy chosen and the type of expenses you are seeking, cover may be available under the policy benefits.

The Overseas Emergency Medical and Hospital Expenses benefit may be able to provide cover for the reimbursement of the reasonable overseas emergency medical, or hospital expenses incurred by you during your trip until you get back to Australia if you become unexpectedly injured in an accident while driving your friend’s car overseas.

Cover is not available in certain scenarios such as (but not limited to):

- If you were racing or were in a competition of any sort
- If your claim arises from you being in control of a motor vehicle without a current Australian driver’s license
- If you claim arises directly or indirectly from you using alcohol or drugs (unless the drugs have been prescribed by your medical practitioner)

Eligibility criteria, policy terms, conditions, exclusions, limits and sub limits apply. Consider the PDS prior to deciding on which policy is right for you and your needs.

Any advice is general advice only and does not take into account your individual objectives, financial situation, or needs. Please consider the PDS before making any decisions regarding the purchase of travel insurance.

As each individual’s circumstances are different, we will assess each claim on a case-by-case basis in accordance with your specific circumstances, policy terms, and Certificate of Insurance.

### Does travel insurance cover me if my travel agent goes out of business?

If your travel agent experiences financial collapse, there is no cover under Fast Cover travel insurance policies for any losses that arise. This means that costs such as prepaid bookings or deposits made through the travel agent would not be reimbursed under your policy.

Every claim is reviewed individually on a case-by-case basis and will only be paid if it meets the terms, conditions, limits, and exclusions in your policy. Always check the PDS carefully so you know exactly what’s included before you travel.

*Source: <https://fastcover.com.au/faq/does-travel-insurance-cover-me-if-my-travel-agent-goes-out-of-business>*

### Does travel insurance cover me if I buy a policy after a natural disaster has already happened?

If you purchase a travel insurance policy after a natural disaster has already occurred, there is no cover for claims related to that event. This is because the natural disaster is considered a *known event* at the time you bought your policy.

Travel insurance is designed to cover unexpected and unforeseen events. Once an event is widely reported in the media or by government and official bodies, it is no longer considered unforeseen, and claims arising from it are excluded.

Every claim is reviewed individually on a case-by-case basis and will only be paid if it meets the terms, conditions, limits, and exclusions in your policy. Always check the PDS carefully so you know exactly what’s included before you travel.

### Does travel insurance cover me if there is an airport strike?

You may be covered if your travel is disrupted due to an unexpected airport strike, as long as the strike was not a known event when you purchased your policy. This means that if a strike occurs after you have bought your cover and it affects your flights, you may be able to claim certain benefits depending on your policy type.

If the strike was already announced or widely reported before you purchased your policy, it would be considered a known event and cover would not apply.

Every claim is reviewed individually on a case-by-case basis and will only be paid if it meets the terms, conditions, limits, and exclusions in your policy. Always check the PDS carefully so you know exactly what’s included before you travel.

Travel insurance with Fast Cover does **not provide cover** for alternative accommodation costs if you need to move due to bed bugs or other insect infestations. For full details, please refer to the PDS.

Every claim is reviewed individually on a case-by-case basis and will only be paid if it meets the terms, conditions, limits, and exclusions in your policy. Always check the PDS carefully so you know exactly what’s included before you travel.

### Does travel insurance cover me if war breaks out in the country I am visiting?

Travel insurance does not provide cover for any loss, damage, or expenses that arise from an act of war. This applies whether the war is declared or not, and also includes situations involving rebellion, revolution, insurrection, or the taking of power by the military.

*Source: <https://fastcover.com.au/faq/does-travel-insurance-cover-me-if-war-breaks-out-in-the-country-i-am-visiting>*

### Does travel insurance cover miscarriage while overseas?

Pregnancy related conditions, including miscarriage, may be covered in certain situations, provided the pregnancy meets the policy conditions. Generally, cover may apply for overseas emergency medical and hospital expenses related to a miscarriage, as long as the pregnancy has not exceeded the gestational limits stated in the PDS and the condition is not considered a known or existing medical condition under the policy definitions.

The PDS also outlines that routine pregnancy care, childbirth, and complications arising after the specified gestation period are not covered. If a miscarriage occurs as a result of an excluded event or condition, such as participation in an excluded activity or an existing medical condition that has not been assessed or covered, related claims may not be payable.

Cover depends on factors such as the stage of pregnancy, your medical history, the reason for treatment, and whether all policy terms, conditions, limits, and exclusions have been met.

Every claim is reviewed individually on a case-by-case basis and will only be paid if it meets the terms, conditions, limits, and exclusions in your policy. Always check the PDS carefully so you know exactly what’s included before you travel.

*Source: <https://fastcover.com.au/faq/does-travel-insurance-cover-miscarriage-while-overseas>*

### Does travel insurance cover childbirth overseas?

Under Fast Cover Travel Insurance, childbirth itself is not covered. This means labour, delivery, routine antenatal care, postnatal care, and costs relating to the newborn are generally excluded.

The PDS does allow for limited cover for unexpected pregnancy related medical emergencies that occur before the gestational limit stated in the policy. These are situations where urgent medical treatment is required due to an unforeseen complication, rather than planned or routine pregnancy care. Once the pregnancy reaches the gestation limit outlined in the PDS, pregnancy related claims are not covered.

Every claim is reviewed individually on a case-by-case basis and will only be paid if it meets the terms, conditions, limits, and exclusions in your policy. Always check the PDS carefully so you know exactly what’s included before you travel.

*Source: <https://fastcover.com.au/faq/does-travel-insurance-cover-childbirth-overseas>*

Fast Cover travel insurance does not provide cover for Trip Cancellation Expenses if your employer cancels your leave. For full details, please refer to the PDS.

Every claim is reviewed individually on a case-by-case basis and will only be paid if it meets the terms, conditions, limits, and exclusions in your policy. Always check the PDS carefully so you know exactly what’s included before you travel.

### Does travel insurance cover my hospital bills if I get sick or injured in Argentina?

Regardless of the travel insurance policy that you choose for your overseas trip to Argentina, one important benefit we include with all our international policies is the Overseas Emergency Medical and Hospital Expenses benefit. Since Australia doesn’t have a Reciprocal Health Care Agreement with Argentina, you’ll likely be responsible for all your medical expenses if you unexpectedly fall sick or are injured while travelling in Argentina. Having cover for these unexpected medical situations during your travels can potentially save you thousands of dollars.

This benefit provides some protection against the financial burden of unexpected medical emergencies that can happen on your trip to Argentina, from food poisoning, treatment for a broken bone or emergency surgery for appendicitis. You should be aware that cover isn’t available for all medical expenses, and some of these include (but are not limited to):

- medical emergencies related to your existing medical conditions which aren’t listed as covered on your certificate of insurance,
- planned medical procedures or other non-emergency medical treatments,
- routine medical or dental check-ups,
- injuries sustained from your participation in sport or leisure activities covered under the Adventure Pack or snow sports unless you’ve purchased additional cover for them, and
- your medical expenses once you’ve returned to Australia,

so it’s important to review your policy to understand what is and isn't covered while you're in Argentina and the terms and conditions that apply.

You can apply for cover for your existing medical conditions and any changes in health and/or new medical conditions you may develop between the time you purchase your policy and the date you depart on your trip to Argentina, through a medical screening. Find out more about what we consider to be a medical condition and how you can apply for cover in our **Travel Insurance for Existing Medical Conditions** page.

As each individual’s circumstances are different, we will assess each claim on a case by case basis and in accordance with your specific circumstances, policy terms and Certificate of Insurance.

Any advice is general advice only and does not take into account your individual objectives, financial situation or needs. Consider the PDS as eligibility criteria, policy terms, conditions, exclusions and limits apply.

*Source: <https://fastcover.com.au/faq/does-travel-insurance-cover-my-hospital-bills-if-i-get-sick-or-injured-in-argentina>*

### Does travel insurance cover heli-skiing or snowboarding?

Heli-skiing and snowboarding are not automatically covered under Fast Cover’s Travel Insurance policies. Only travellers aged 69 and under at the date of policy issue may have cover for heli-skiing and snowboarding (including backcountry heli-skiing and snowboarding) if:

- They have purchased a Domestic Plus or Snow Sports Plus policy,
- The heli-skiing and snowboarding are done with a professional snow sport instructor, and
- The heli-skiing and snowboarding are provided by a commercial operator and available to the general public only.

Cover is not available for heli-skiing or snowboarding in the backcountry without a professional snow sport instructor.

For more information about how our Snow Sports cover relates to heli-skiing or snowboarding, read our PDS to learn more about what is covered and what is not covered.

### Does travel insurance cover my hospital bills if I get sick or injured in Europe?

Australia has Reciprocal Health Care Agreements (RHCA) with some countries in Europe including [**Belgium**](https://www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/reciprocal-health-care-agreement-visiting-belgium?context=22481), [**Finland**](https://www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/reciprocal-health-care-agreement-visiting-finland?context=22481), [**Italy**](https://www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/reciprocal-health-care-agreement-visiting-italy?context=22481), [**Malta**](https://www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/reciprocal-health-care-agreement-visiting-malta?context=22481), [**the Netherlands**](https://www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/reciprocal-health-care-agreement-visiting-netherlands?context=22481), [**Norway**](https://www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/reciprocal-health-care-agreement-visiting-norway?context=22481), the [**Republic of Ireland**](https://www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/reciprocal-health-care-agreement-visiting-republic-ireland?context=22481), [**Slovenia**](https://www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/reciprocal-health-care-agreement-visiting-slovenia?context=22481), [**Sweden**](https://www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/reciprocal-health-care-agreement-visiting-sweden?context=22481) and the [**United Kingdom**](https://www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/reciprocal-health-care-agreement-visiting-united-kingdom?context=22481), meaning you may have some cover for medical costs in the public health system of that country through the agreement. Fast Cover’s travel insurance policy will not pay for the cost of medical care that is covered by the RHCA between Australia and the relevant country.

However, Reciprocal Health Care Agreements do not cover every type of medical expenses, so taking out a Fast Cover travel insurance policy for Europe with medical cover for **unexpected overseas emergency medical and hospital expenses**, **overseas emergency dental**, and [**overseas emergency medical evacuation and repatriation**](../travel-insurance-guide/overseas-emergency-medical-evacuation-and-repatriation) may provide you with cover if you unexpectedly fall sick or become injured while travelling in Europe, where cover is not available under a relevant RHCA. Having cover for these unexpected medical situations during your travel to Europe can potentially save you thousands of dollars.

The benefit of overseas emergency medical and hospital expenses provides some protection against the financial burden of unexpected medical emergencies that can happen on your trip to Europe, from food poisoning, treatment for a broken bone or emergency surgery for appendicitis, particularly if this occurs after a certain number of months of your arrival to a country with which Australia has a Reciprocal Health Care Agreement. You should be aware that cover isn’t available for all medical expenses, and some of these may include (but are not limited to):

- medical emergencies related to your existing medical conditions which aren’t listed as covered on your certificate of insurance,
- planned medical procedures or other non-emergency medical treatments,
- routine medical or dental check-ups,
- injuries sustained from your participation in sport or leisure activities covered under the Adventure Pack or snow sports unless you’ve added them to your policy and paid an additional premium to include cover for them, and
- your medical expenses once you’ve returned to Australia,

so it’s important to review your policy to understand what is and isn't covered while you're in Europe and the terms and conditions that apply.

You can apply for cover for your existing medical conditions and any changes in health and/or new medical conditions you may develop between the time you purchase your policy and the date you depart on your trip to Europe through a medical screening. Find out more about what we consider to be a medical condition and how you can apply for cover in our **Travel Insurance for existing Medical Conditions** page. ^

As each individual’s circumstances are different, we will assess each claim on a case by case basis and in accordance with your specific circumstances, policy terms and Certificate of Insurance.

Any advice is general advice only and does not take into account your individual objectives, financial situation or needs. Consider the PDS as eligibility criteria, policy terms, conditions, exclusions and limits apply.

*Source: <https://fastcover.com.au/faq/does-travel-insurance-cover-my-hospital-bills-if-i-get-sick-or-injured-in-europe>*

### Does travel insurance cover missed international flights due to a cancelled or delayed domestic flight?

If your domestic flight gets cancelled or delayed and you end up missing your international flight or cruise, you may be covered under your Fast Cover policy, it just depends on the level of cover you’ve chosen and the situation.

Here’s how cover may apply:

- Special Event Transport Expenses: May cover reasonable extra travel costs to get you to an overseas special event on time if your transport is cancelled, delayed, or diverted. Available under Comprehensive, Snow Sports Plus, Domestic Plus, and Frequent Traveller Saver policies.
- Trip Cancellation Expenses: May cover non-refundable prepaid costs if your trip is cancelled, delayed, or rescheduled and that you have paid in advance and cannot recover in any other way. Available under Comprehensive, Snow Sports Plus, Domestic Plus, Frequent Traveller Saver, and Standard Saver policies.
- Trip Disruption Expenses: Can help with reasonable additional accommodation and travel cost if your scheduled or connecting transport is disrupted after your trip has started due to circumstances outside your control (such as airline delays because of severe weather). Available under Comprehensive, Snow Sports Plus, Domestic Plus, and Frequent Traveller Saver, Standard Saver policies.
- Travel Delay Expenses: May cover reasonable additional meals and accommodation if your scheduled transport is delayed by more than 6 hours. Available under Comprehensive, Snow Sports Plus, Domestic Plus, and Frequent Traveller Saver policies.

Every claim is reviewed individually on a case-by-case basis and will only be paid if it meets the terms, conditions, limits, and exclusions in your policy. Always check the PDS carefully so you know exactly what’s included before you travel.

*Source: <https://fastcover.com.au/faq/does-travel-insurance-cover-missed-international-flights-due-to-a-cancelled-or-delayed-domestic-flight>*

### Does travel insurance cover my bicycle if it’s damaged in transit?

Bicycles can be covered under your travel insurance if you’ve added the Bicycle Pack to your policy and it’s shown on your Certificate of Insurance. To be eligible, your bike needs to be:

- Less than three years old; and
- Valued at $1500 or more; and
- Free of defects.

Just a heads-up, the Bicycle Pack is not available with the Basics policy.

Every claim is reviewed individually on case-by-case basis and will only be paid if it meets the terms, conditions, limits, and exclusions of your policy. Be sure to check the PDS so you know exactly what’s covered before you travel.

Since Australia doesn’t currently have a Reciprocal Health Care Agreement with any country in South America, you’ll likely be responsible for all your medical expenses if you unexpectedly fall sick or are injured while travelling in South America. Having cover for these unexpected medical situations during your travels can potentially save you thousands of dollars.

This benefit provides some protection against the financial burden of unexpected medical emergencies that can happen on your trip to South America, from food poisoning, treatment for a broken bone or emergency surgery for appendicitis. You should be aware that cover isn’t available for all medical expenses, and some of these include (but are not limited to):

- medical emergencies related to your existing medical conditions which aren’t listed as covered on your certificate of insurance,
- planned medical procedures or other non-emergency medical treatments,
- routine medical or dental check-ups,
- injuries sustained from your participation in sport or leisure activities covered under the Adventure Pack or snow sports unless you’ve purchased additional cover for them, and
- your medical expenses once you’ve returned to Australia,

so it’s important to review your policy to understand what is and isn't covered while you're in South America and the terms and conditions that apply.

You can apply for cover for your existing medical conditions and any changes in health and/or new medical conditions you may develop between the time you purchase your policy and the date you depart on your trip to South America through a medical screening. Find out more about what we consider to be a medical condition and how you can apply for cover in our **Travel Insurance for Existing Medical Conditions** page.

As each individual’s circumstances are different, we will assess each claim on a case by case basis and in accordance with your specific circumstances, policy terms and Certificate of Insurance.

Any advice is general advice only and does not take into account your individual objectives, financial situation or needs. Consider the PDS as eligibility criteria, policy terms, conditions, exclusions and limits apply.

*Source: <https://fastcover.com.au/faq/does-travel-insurance-cover-my-hospital-bills-if-i-get-sick-or-injured-in-south-america>*

### Does travel insurance cover my hospital bills if I get sick or injured in Ireland?

Australia has a [**Reciprocal Health Care Agreement (RHCA) with the Republic of Ireland**](https://www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/reciprocal-health-care-agreement-visiting-republic-ireland?context=22481), meaning you may have some cover for medical costs in the Irish public health system through the agreement. Fast Cover’s travel insurance policy will not pay for the cost of medical care that is covered by the RHCA between Australia and Ireland. However, the RHCA does not cover every type of medical expenses, so taking out a Fast Cover travel insurance policy for Ireland with medical cover for [**unexpected overseas emergency medical and hospital expenses**](../travel-insurance-guide/overseas-emergency-medical-and-hospital-expenses), [**overseas emergency dental**](../travel-insurance-guide/overseas-emergency-dental), and [**overseas emergency medical evacuation and repatriation**](../travel-insurance-guide/overseas-emergency-medical-evacuation-and-repatriation) may provide you with cover if you unexpectedly fall sick or become injured while travelling in Ireland where cover is not available under the RHCA. Having cover for these unexpected medical situations during your travels can potentially save you thousands of dollars.

The benefit of overseas emergency medical and hospital expenses provides some protection against the financial burden of unexpected medical emergencies that can happen on your trip to Ireland, from food poisoning, treatment for a broken bone or emergency surgery for appendicitis, particularly if this occurs after 12 months of your arrival to Ireland. You should be aware that cover isn’t available for all medical expenses, and some of these may include (but are not limited to):

- medical emergencies related to your existing medical conditions which aren’t listed as covered on your certificate of insurance,
- planned medical procedures or other non-emergency medical treatments,
- routine medical or dental check-ups,
- injuries sustained from your participation in sport or leisure activities covered under the Adventure Pack or snow sports unless you’ve added them to your policy and paid an additional premium to include cover for them, and
- your medical expenses once you’ve returned to Australia,

so it’s important to review your policy to understand what is and isn't covered while you're in Ireland and the terms and conditions that apply.

You can apply for cover for your existing medical conditions and any changes in health and/or new medical conditions you may develop between the time you purchase your policy and the date you depart on your trip to Ireland through a medical screening. Find out more about what we consider to be a medical condition and how you can apply for cover in our **Travel Insurance for existing Medical Conditions** page.

As each individual’s circumstances are different, we will assess each claim on a case by case basis and in accordance with your specific circumstances, policy terms and Certificate of Insurance.

### Does travel insurance cover my missed domestic flight if my international flight home is delayed?

A domestic flight that connects with your international trip may be considered part of your holiday, as long as the date is included in your policy and you have listed **‘Australia’** as part of your travel destination.

If your international flight back to Australia is delayed and you miss your domestic connection, you may be covered. Whether a claim is payable will depend on the **reason for the delay or cancellation** and the terms of your policy.

Every claim is reviewed individually on a case-by-case basis and will only be paid if it meets the terms, conditions, limits, and exclusions in your policy. Always check the PDS carefully so you know exactly what’s included before you travel.

### Does travel insurance cover passport replacement if it’s accidentally damaged?

If your passport is lost, stolen, or accidentally damaged during your trip, you may be able to claim the reasonable replacement costs, including associated communication costs, under the Passports, Credit Cards, and Credit Card Fraud benefit.

Please note that this benefit is only available under the Comprehensive, Standard Saver, Snow Sports Plus and Frequent Traveller Saver Policy.

Every claim is reviewed individually on a case-by-case basis and will only be paid if it meets the terms, conditions, limits, and exclusions in your policy. Always check the PDS carefully so you know exactly what’s included before you travel.

### Does travel insurance cover prepaid theme park tickets?

Prepaid theme park tickets can be something you’re able to claim for when they’re part of your prebooked and pre-paid trip costs that you can’t recover in any other way.

This type of claim is generally considered when you have to unexpectedly cancel or reschedule before your trip starts, or you have to shorten your trip and cancel remaining prepaid bookings while you’re away. You’ll also need to make a reasonable effort to recover any refundable tickets or credits first, as anything you can get back is taken off the claim amount.

It’s important to note that you cannot claim if the theme park itself closes or changes its schedule for reasons outside of your policy cover, or if you simply change your mind about attending.

Every claim is reviewed individually on a case-by-case basis and will only be paid if it meets the terms, conditions, limits, and exclusions in your policy. Always check the PDS carefully so you know exactly what’s included before you travel.

*Source: <https://fastcover.com.au/faq/does-travel-insurance-cover-prepaid-theme-park-tickets>*

### Does travel insurance cover my hospital bills if I get sick or injured in Peru?

Regardless of the travel insurance policy that you choose for your overseas trip to Peru, one important benefit we include with all our international policies is the Overseas Emergency Medical and Hospital Expenses benefit. Since Australia doesn’t have a Reciprocal Health Care Agreement with Peru, you’ll likely be responsible for all your medical expenses if you unexpectedly fall sick or are injured while travelling in Peru. Having cover for these unexpected medical situations during your travels can potentially save you thousands of dollars.

This benefit provides some protection against the financial burden of unexpected medical emergencies that can happen on your trip to Peru, from food poisoning, treatment for a broken bone or emergency surgery for appendicitis. You should be aware that cover isn’t available for all medical expenses, and some of these include (but are not limited to):

- medical emergencies related to your existing medical conditions which aren’t listed as covered on your certificate of insurance,
- planned medical procedures or other non-emergency medical treatments,
- routine medical or dental check-ups,
- injuries sustained from your participation in sport or leisure activities covered under the Adventure Pack or snow sports unless you’ve purchased additional cover for them, and
- your medical expenses once you’ve returned to Australia,

so it’s important to review your policy to understand what is and isn't covered while you're in Peru and the terms and conditions that apply.

You can apply for cover for your existing medical conditions and any changes in health and/or new medical conditions you may develop between the time you purchase your policy and the date you depart on your trip to Peru through a medical screening. Find out more about what we consider to be a medical condition and how you can apply for cover in our **Travel Insurance for Existing Medical Conditions** page.

As each individual’s circumstances are different, we will assess each claim on a case by case basis and in accordance with your specific circumstances, policy terms and Certificate of Insurance.

Any advice is general advice only and does not take into account your individual objectives, financial situation or needs. Consider the PDS as eligibility criteria, policy terms, conditions, exclusions and limits apply.

*Source: <https://fastcover.com.au/faq/does-travel-insurance-cover-my-hospital-bills-if-i-get-sick-or-injured-in-peru>*

### Does travel insurance cover riding a motorcycle overseas?

Travel insurance with Fast Cover can provide cover for riding a motorcycle overseas, but only if you have purchased the Motorcycle Pack as an optional add-on. Without this pack, there is no cover for riding or being a passenger on a motorcycle.

To be eligible for cover, you must:

- You must be aged 74 and under at the date of policy issue to purchase the Motorcycle Pack.
- If you are rider of a motorcycle of engine capacity of 125cc or less, you must hold both a current Australian Drivers Licence (Provisional or higher) (regardless of the local laws) and a licence valid for the country that you are riding in.
- If you are rider of a motorcycle of engine capacity greater than 125cc, you must hold both a current Australian Motorcycle Licence (Provisional or higher) valid for the same class of motorcycle (regardless of the local laws) and a licence valid for the country that you are riding in.
- If you are the passenger on a motorcycle the person in control must hold a current licence (Provisional or higher) valid for the same class of motorcycle valid for the country that you are in. Follow the Australian licensing rules that apply to your licence type
- Meet the licensing requirements of the country you are visiting
- Wear a helmet at all times while riding

Cover may not extend to all motorcycle activities, and exclusions apply, particularly for racing or professional use. Always review the Product Disclosure Statement (PDS) for full details of what is and isn’t covered under the Motorcycle Pack.

Every claim is reviewed individually on a case-by-case basis and will only be paid if it meets the terms, conditions, limits, and exclusions in your policy. Always check the PDS carefully so you know exactly what’s included before you travel.

### Does travel insurance cover volcanic ash clouds?

Fast Cover travel insurance may provide cover if your trip is disrupted or you are injured due to a volcanic ash cloud. The level of cover depends on the type of policy you have chosen:

- **Medical cover**: Comprehensive, Snow Sports Plus, Standard Saver, Frequent Traveller Saver, and Basics policies may provide medical cover if you are injured as a result of the natural disaster.
- **Travel and accommodation arrangements**: Comprehensive, Snow Sports Plus, Standard Saver, Frequent Traveller Saver, and Domestic Plus policies may provide cover towards additional costs if your scheduled or connecting transport is cancelled, delayed, rescheduled, or diverted due to a natural disaster.
- **Travel delays and special event transport**: Comprehensive, Snow Sports Plus, Frequent Traveller Saver, and Domestic Plus policies may provide cover if your transport disruption causes delays or impacts special event connections.

Whether cover applies may also depend on:

- If the volcanic ash cloud was unforeseen when you booked your travel.
- When you purchased your travel insurance policy.
- Whether your travel took place against the advice or warnings of a government, official body, or widely reported media warnings about the natural disaster.

Every claim is reviewed individually on a case-by-case basis and will only be paid if it meets the terms, conditions, limits, and exclusions in your policy. Always check the PDS carefully so you know exactly what’s included before you travel.
