### Does travel insurance cover pregnancy?

Fast Cover travel insurance can include cover for unexpected serious complications of pregnancy and childbirth that occur.

- Up to the end of the 23rd week of pregnancy if You are pregnant with a single child; or
- Up to the end of the 19th week of pregnancy if You are pregnant with twins or multiple children.

We do not provide cover for:

- Any claim related to pregnancy after these timeframes
- Childbirth, unless due to a complication listed in the PDS and shown as covered on your Certificate on Insurance, or a diagnosis during your trip
- The health or care of a newborn (including premature birth overseas)
- Antenatal care, medications or vitamins

We also do not cover pregnancy conditions that existed:

- In the **3 years before** your policy issue date, or
- Between your policy issue date and departure (except for Trip Cancellation under Benefit 5),

unless we agree to list the condition as covered on your Certificate of Insurance.

If your health changes after a condition has been listed as covered and before departure, cover is automatically excluded unless you complete further medical screening and we agree to continue cover.

Every pregnancy is different, which is why each claim is looked at individually on a case-by-case basis. Claims are only paid if they meet the terms, conditions, limits, and exclusions of your policy. It’s always best to check the PDS so you know exactly what’s included before you travel.

*Source: <https://fastcover.com.au/faq/does-travel-insurance-cover-pregnancy>*

### Does travel insurance cover weather events?

Fast Cover travel insurance may provide cover for unexpected severe weather events that occur after you have purchased your policy and that directly affect your travel plans. This can include disruptions such as cancelled or delayed flights, accommodation issues, or other trip interruptions caused by extreme weather.

Every claim is reviewed individually on a case-by-case basis and will only be paid if it meets the terms, conditions, limits, and exclusions in your policy. Always check the PDS carefully so you know exactly what’s included before you travel.

### Does travel insurance for an IEC trip cover elective dental or medical procedures?

Travel insurance generally does not provide cover for elective or planned dental or medical procedures. Cover is only available for unexpected medical emergencies, accidents, or illnesses that occur while you are travelling, in line with the terms of your policy.

Any elective treatment, including procedures arranged before you travel or scheduled while overseas, might not be covered under the policy. It is important to review the Product Disclosure Statement (PDS) to understand the limits and exclusions that apply to medical and dental treatment.

Every claim is reviewed individually on a case-by-case basis and will only be paid if it meets the terms, conditions, limits, and exclusions in your policy. Always check the PDS carefully so you know exactly what’s included before you travel.

### Does travel insurance cover travellers on a KITAS residence visa?

Travel insurance is usually designed to cover travellers who are intending to come back home to Australia. If you are on a KITAS residence visa and not intending to come home to Australia, you may not be eligible to purchase our travel insurance.

Eligibility depends on your circumstances, such as the length of your trip, your country of residence, and whether your travel is considered temporary or permanent. It is important to check the Product Disclosure Statement (PDS) for the full eligibility requirements and exclusions.

Every claim is reviewed individually on a case-by-case basis and will only be paid if it meets the terms, conditions, limits, and exclusions in your policy. Always check the PDS carefully so you know exactly what’s included before you travel.

### Does travel insurance include GST?

GST (Goods and Services Tax) may apply to your Fast Cover Travel Insurance policy depending on the type of policy and your individual circumstances:

- Domestic Plus Policy and Frequent Traveller Saver Policy: These policies include a GST component because they provide cover for travel within Australia.
- International Travel Insurance Policies: GST generally does not apply because these policies provide cover for travel outside of Australia.

Eligibility criteria, policy terms, conditions, exclusions, limits and sub limits apply. Consider the PDS prior to deciding on which policy is right for you and your needs.

Any advice is general advice only and does not take into account your individual objectives, financial situation, or needs. Please consider the PDS before making any decisions regarding the purchase of travel insurance.

### Does Vietnam have a visa exemption for Australians?

Australians are not eligible for visa-free travel to Vietnam as Australia does not fall under Vietnam’s visa exemption scheme. However, Australians can apply for a visa on arrival once they land in Vietnam, provided they have a pre-arranged and approved Letter of Entry.

As entry and visa requirements for Vietnam may change over time, it is your responsibility to verify visa requirements with the [Vietnamese Embassy](https://www.vietnamembassy.org.au/), your local Vietnamese Consulate, or official government source.

*Source: <https://fastcover.com.au/faq/does-vietnam-have-a-visa-exemption-for-australians>*

### Does your Unlimited Overseas Medical benefit cover ambulance?

The Unlimited Overseas Medical benefit can cover an unlimited amount of costs, including emergency ambulance overseas, provided the emergency relates to a reason you can claim for under your policy. Ambulance services in Australia are not covered.

Every claim is reviewed individually on a case-by-case basis and will only be paid if it meets the terms, conditions, limits, and exclusions in your policy. Always check the PDS carefully so you know exactly what’s included before you travel.

### How am I assured of a fair decision when making a claim?

Fast Cover is committed to fair outcomes for all customers. We adopt the General Insurance Code of Practice, which is designed to raise standards of practice and service across the general insurance industry.

If we do not accept your claim, you can request a review through our formal complaints process:

**For policies purchased on or after 15 October 2026, please follow the below process:**

**Step 1**

Please contact:

Fast Cover Travel Insurance
Email: [info@fastcover.com.au](mailto:info@fastcover.com.au)
Phone: [1300 409 322](tel:1300409322)
Mail: PO Box R1384, Royal Exchange NSW 1225

We will acknowledge receipt of your complaint and we will aim to resolve the complaint to your satisfaction.

A complaint decision will be provided to you within 30 calendar days. If we are unable to meet this timeframe we will inform you of the reason for the delay.

**Step 2**

If your complaint is not resolved to your satisfaction, or you do not receive a complaint decision within 30 calendar days of the date on which you first made the complaint, you can refer your complaint to the Australian Financial Complaints Authority (AFCA). You can contact AFCA as follows:

Phone: 1800 931 678
Email: [info@afca.org.au](mailto:info@afca.org.au)
Website: [www.afca.org.au](http://www.afca.org.au/)
Post: GPO Box 3 Melbourne VIC 3001

AFCA services are provided to you free of charge. Your complaint must be referred to AFCA within 2 years of the complaint decision, unless AFCA considers special circumstances apply. If your complaint is not eligible for consideration by AFCA, you may have access to other external dispute resolution options.

**For policies purchased prior to 15 October 2026, please follow the below process:**

**Stage 1: Contact us**

Inform us of your complaint via phone, email or post. We will acknowledge when we receive your complaint and do our best to resolve it to your satisfaction within 10 business days. If we cannot resolve your complaint within 10 business days, we will provide you with an update every 10 business days, unless you agree to a different timeframe.

Fast Cover Travel Insurance

Phone: 1300 409 322
Email: [info@fastcover.com.au](mailto:info@fastcover.com.au)
Post: PO Box R1384, Royal Exchange NSW 1225

**Stage 2: Complaint Review**

If we cannot resolve your complaint to your satisfaction, we will escalate your complaint to Lloyds Australia. A final decision will be provided to you within 30 days of the date you first made the complaint. If a decision cannot be made within this timeframe, you will be contacted in writing before the deadline with the reason for the delay. You will also be informed of your right to take your complaint to the Australian Financial Complaints Authority (AFCA) and how to do so.

Lloyd’s Australia Limited
Phone: 02 8298 0783
Email: [idraustralia@lloyds.com](mailto:idraustralia@lloyds.com)
Post: PO Box R1745, Royal Exchange NSW 1225

**Stage 3: External review**

If you’re still unhappy with our decision, or if we haven’t responded within 30 days, you can escalate your complaint to the Australian Financial Complaints Authority (AFCA). This is a free and independent service:

- Website: www.afca.org.au
- Email: [info@afca.org.au](mailto:info@afca.org.au)
- Phone: 1800 931 678

AFCA’s decision is binding on us, but not on you. You also retain the right to seek legal assistance if you wish.

*Source: <https://fastcover.com.au/faq/how-am-i-assured-of-a-fair-decision-when-making-a-claim>*

### How are Duo travel insurance quotes calculated?

This makes Duo policies a way for two travellers on the same itinerary to be covered under one policy, instead of buying two separate Single policies.

### Does travel insurance provide cover if I am working overseas?

Travel insurance can still apply if you are working overseas, but cover is usually limited to the benefits listed in your policy, such as overseas medical emergencies, cancellation, and luggage. The policy does not provide cover for every aspect of employment.

There might be no cover for loss of income if your job ends early, no cover for workplace liability, and no cover for work-related equipment or tools.

Before travelling, it is important to review the Product Disclosure Statement (PDS) to check what is included and excluded when working overseas, and to consider whether separate business or employment-related insurance is needed.

Every claim is reviewed individually on a case-by-case basis and will only be paid if it meets the terms, conditions, limits, and exclusions in your policy. Always check the PDS carefully so you know exactly what’s included before you travel.

*Source: <https://fastcover.com.au/faq/does-travel-insurance-provide-cover-if-i-am-working-overseas>*

### How do I get a quote for multiple countries in one trip?

When getting a quote for travel to multiple countries, you will need to list all of those countries. Alternatively, select one of the four geographical regions: South Pacific, Asia, Europe and/or Worldwide that covers all the destinations you’ll be visiting.

Each country falls within a set region, and your policy will only apply to the region chosen. Refer to the website to see the list of countries covered in each region at fastcover.com.au/regions. A copy of the Countries/Destinations list can be downloaded from www.fastcover.com.au/regions, or obtained from Fast Cover, on request, at no extra charge. Cover is only available for the countries or region You have selected at the time of purchase and listed on your Certificate of insurance.

If your trip includes - transit in another country or region, you automatically have cover for up to 48 hours while in transit. But if you plan to leave the airport or stay in that country or region, you’ll need to select that country or region at the time you purchase your policy for full cover.

For help confirming which region applies to your trip, you can contact our team before purchasing your policy.

Every claim is reviewed individually on a case-by-case basis and will only be paid if it meets the terms, conditions, limits, and exclusions in your policy. Always check the PDS carefully so you know exactly what’s included before you travel.

### How do I know if I need to take out a cruise policy?

We consider a ‘cruise ship’ to be a commercially operated ocean-going vessel that is licensed to carry paying passengers, has on-board accommodation and a trained medical practitioner or staff trained and accredited in advanced first aid (or the equivalent level in the country that you are travelling in).

You must specify Cruise cover at time of purchase if you will be travelling on a cruise ship and you are cruising in:

- Australian waters, the New Zealand or the South Pacific Region for 1 night or more, or
- Asia, Europe or Worldwide Regions for 4 nights or more.

Eligibility criteria, policy terms, conditions, exclusions and limits apply. Consider the PDS prior to deciding on which policy is right for you and your needs.

*Source: <https://fastcover.com.au/faq/how-do-i-know-if-i-need-to-take-out-a-cruise-policy>*

### How do I make a travel insurance claim?

If you need medical, hospital, or dental help while you’re away, please get in touch straight away so we can assist with your care and confirm any pre-approved expenses.

For loss or theft of your luggage and personal effects make sure you report it to the police as soon as practicable, but preferably within 24 hours and ask for a written report.

For damage or misplacement of your luggage and personal effects caused by the airline or any other operator or accommodation provider, report the damage or misplacement to an appropriate official as soon as practicable, but preferably within 24 hours of discovering the loss and obtain a written report, including any offer of settlement that they may make.

To support your claim, you may be asked to provide documents such as receipts, police reports, or medical records. Depending on the situation, we may repair, replace, or reimburse you for the item’s value (minus depreciation). Payments are made in Australian dollars to your nominated bank account. The rate of currency exchange that will apply is the rate on the date You incurred the expense or suffered the loss, as applicable.

Every claim is assessed individually on case-by-case basis and will only be paid if it meets the terms, conditions, limits, and exclusions of your policy. Check the PDS so you know exactly what’s covered before you travel.

### How do I report Fraud?

Submitting an insurance claim that is not true, correct, or for an event that did not occur, is misleading or exaggerated might be an offence under Australian Law and might lead to prosecution.

If you submit a claim which is fraudulent, or false in any respect, or there is a material alteration in the risk, we may deny part of, or all of the claim, to the extent permitted by law. If you, or someone authorised as acting for you, submits to us any false or misleading information you may be prosecuted. Additionally, your policy may be cancelled by us and no refund of premium will be made.

Insurance fraud and fraudulent claims force the cost of your insurance to increase. For the community and your benefit, we encourage you to assist in reducing insurance fraud by reporting it:

- Via email to [info@fastcover.com.au](mailto:info@fastcover.com.au)
- By calling [1300 409 322](../contact) during our business hours

All information will be treated with full confidentiality and protected to the full extent of the law.

*Source: <https://fastcover.com.au/faq/how-do-i-report-fraud>*

### How do sub limits work if I have the Basics policy with 2,000 of luggage cover?

If you’ve added the optional luggage cover to your Basics policy, you’re covered for up to $2,000 in total for all your luggage and personal items combined. Sub limits still apply, which means each type of item has its own maximum amount you can claim within that overall $2,000 limit.

For example, the standard sub limits include amounts such as:

- up to $1,500 for mobile phones and other portable communication devices
- up to $1,000 for tablets
- up to $3,000 for stand-alone cameras and video recorders
- up to $750 for any other unspecified item or set

These sub limits apply even if you haven’t reached your total $2,000 policy limit.

If you need higher cover for an individual item, you can upgrade your policy to a higher level of cover.

Your Certificate of Insurance will show exactly what applies to your policy.

Every claim is reviewed individually on a case-by-case basis and will only be paid if it meets the terms, conditions, limits, and exclusions in your policy. Always check the PDS carefully so you know exactly what’s included before you travel.

*Source: <https://fastcover.com.au/faq/how-do-sub-limits-work-if-i-have-the-basics-policy-with-2-000-of-luggage-cover>*

### How does Fast Cover car rental excess cover work?

Fast Cover can cover rental vehicle insurance excess on eligible policies, either automatically included or available as an optional extra, depending on the policy you choose.

- Overseas: Rental Vehicle Excess cover isn’t automatically included, but you can choose to add it (and pay an additional premium). If added, it can cover rental vehicle excess up to $8,000 (as shown on your Certificate of Insurance). The optional add-on can be added under our Snow Sports Plus, Frequent Traveller Saver, Comprehensive, and Standard Saver policy.
- Domestic (Australia): Our Domestic Plus policy includes Rental Vehicle Excess cover up to $5,000.

If this benefit applies to your policy, it may reimburse the excess amount you become liable to pay after an insured event, up to the limit on your Certificate of Insurance, provided you meet all terms in the PDS.

This benefit doesn’t replace the rental company’s insurance and generally only applies to the excess portion.

- The benefit limits provided under each policy in the 'Benefit Summary' table, when we will pay a claim under each Benefit section applicable to the cover you choose and any endorsements under the 'Optional Cover' section (remember, certain words have special meanings - see the 'Words with Special Meanings' section in the [PDS](https://fastcover.com.au/pds));
- 'Important Matters' - this contains important information on Your Certificate of Insurance, the period of insurance and extensions of cover, your Duty of Disclosure (including how the Duty applies to you and what happens if you breach the Duty), cooling off period, Financial Claims Scheme and the dispute resolution process;
- When we will not pay a claim under each Benefit section applicable to the cover you choose and the General Exclusions that apply to all Benefits (this restricts the cover and benefits); and
- 'What You need to do when making a Claim' - this details what to need to do when making a claim and sets out certain obligations that you and we have. If you do not meet them we may refuse to pay a claim.

### How do I get a 2-year travel insurance policy for the IEC program?

Travel insurance from Fast Cover is initially issued as a 12-month policy. You may be able to extend it for up to a further 12 months by paying an additional premium within 30 days prior to your departure date.

You can extend your policy in two ways:

- Log in to your policy through the Fast Cover website on Fast Cover - Your Policy Login Page and request the extension. Your cover dates will update once you have paid the additional premium, and you will be able to download a new Certificate of Insurance with the revised dates.
- Contact Fast Cover by phone on 1300 409 322 or reply to your policy confirmation email to arrange the extension.

The combined length of the original policy and the extension cannot exceed 24 months in total.

Please note that Fast Cover does not determine if your travel insurance policy meets IEC health insurance requirements. As IEC entry requirements may change over time, it is your responsibility to verify whether the medical coverage on your chosen travel insurance policy meets the IEC health insurance requirement. It is recommended to consult the IRCC or Canadian embassy for specific details.

Every claim is reviewed individually on a case-by-case basis and will only be paid if it meets the terms, conditions, limits, and exclusions in your policy. Always check the PDS carefully so you know exactly what’s included before you travel.

### How is my premium calculated?

Your premium is shown on your Certificate of Insurance. It’s calculated when you first purchase your policy, and again if you make changes or extend your cover.

The premium is calculated based on a number of factors, including:

- The policy you have chosen,
- Your age,
- Where you are going to,
- The length of your trip,
- Existing medical conditions
- The time between purchase and departure
- Any add-ons you have chosen.

*Source: <https://fastcover.com.au/faq/how-is-my-premium-calculated>*

### How long am I covered for?

The period of coverage under your Fast Cover Travel Insurance is specified in your Certificate of Insurance and varies depending on the type of policy you have purchased and the duration of your trip.

#### Cover Period for Policies Purchased Before You Depart Australia:

For Comprehensive, Snow Sports Plus, Standard Saver, and Domestic Plus Policies:

- The cover for Benefit 5: Trip Cancellation Expenses begins from the time the policy is issued.
- Cover for all other benefits begins on the departure date specified on your Certificate of Insurance.

For Basics Policies:

- Cover for all benefits begins on the date of departure as stated on your Certificate of Insurance.
- There is no Trip Cancellation Expenses coverage before the departure date under a Basics policy.

For Frequent Traveller Saver Policies:

- The cover for Benefit 5: Trip Cancellation Expenses begins from the start date specified on your Certificate of Insurance.
- Cover for all other benefits begins on the date of departure for each trip.

#### Cover Period for Policies Purchased while already Overseas:

- There is no cover under any benefit for the first 48 hours from the time the policy is issued. This is known as your "no-cover period." This means there is no cover arising from events that happen within the 48 hour no-cover period for all benefits under the policy, , except under:
- Benefit 27: COVID-19 Overseas Emergency Medical, Hospital, and Medical Evacuation Expenses, where there isa a 72 hour no-cover period from the time the policy is issued; and
- Benefit 28: COVID-19 Trip Cancellation and Disruption, where there isa a 72 hour no-cover period from the time the policy is issued.
- Coverage for all benefits begins immediately following the no-cover period and continues until the return date specified on your Certificate of Insurance.

#### For All Policies:

- Cover ends on the date of return set out on your Certificate of Insurance or when the policy otherwise ends in accordance with its terms, whichever happens first.
- The state listed on your Certificate of Insurance determines the time zone used to determine your policy's purchase date, departure date, and end date.
- If you return home early for any reason:
- Coverage is suspended from the time you return home until you leave home to continue your trip.
- You must have at least 14 days remaining of the period of insurance as noted on your Certificate of Insurance to resume your trip.
- Following the resumption of your trip, your policy will remain valid until the end date shown on your Certificate of Insurance or your permanent return home, whichever comes first.
- Fast Cover will not pay any costs for your return to Australia unless the costs are covered by your policy.

It is important to review the Product Disclosure Statement before making any decisions to ensure the policy is suitable for your needs.

Any advice is general advice only and does not take into account your individual objectives, financial situation, or needs. Please consider the PDS before making any decisions regarding the purchase of travel insurance.

### How long can Australians stay in Malaysia visa-free?

Currently, Australian passport holders can stay in Malaysia for up to 90 days without a visa under the visa exemption arrangement for tourism or business purposes. This period begins from the date of entry and is not extendable under the visa-free scheme. If you need to stay longer, you should apply for the appropriate entry permit before your travel.

Any advice is general advice only and does not take into account your individual objectives, financial situation, or needs. As entry and visa requirements for Malaysia may change over time, it is your responsibility to verify entry and visa requirements with the official government authorities including the [**Malaysian Immigration Department**](https://www.imi.gov.my/index.php/en/), the [**Ministry of Foreign Affairs Malaysia**](https://www.kln.gov.my/), and the [**High Commission of Malaysia in Australia**](https://www.kln.gov.my/web/aus_canberra).

*Source: <https://fastcover.com.au/faq/how-long-can-australians-stay-in-malaysia-visa-free>*

### How do I make a complaint about my Fast Cover travel insurance policy or experience?

We treat complaints seriously and want to resolve them as fast as we can.

If you have any concerns or wish to make a complaint in relation to our policy, our services or your insurance claim, please let us know and we will attempt to resolve your concerns in accordance with our Internal Dispute Resolution procedure.

**For policies purchased on or after 15 October 2026, please follow the below process:**

#### Step 1

Please contact:

Fast Cover Travel Insurance
Email: [info@fastcover.com.au](mailto:info@fastcover.com.au)
Phone: [1300 409 322](tel:1300409322)
Mail: PO Box R1384, Royal Exchange NSW 1225

We will acknowledge receipt of your complaint and we will aim to resolve the complaint to your satisfaction.

A complaint decision will be provided to you within 30 calendar days. If we are unable to meet this timeframe we will inform you of the reason for the delay.

#### Step 2

If your complaint is not resolved to your satisfaction, or you do not receive a complaint decision within 30 calendar days of the date on which you first made the complaint, you can refer your complaint to the Australian Financial Complaints Authority (AFCA). You can contact AFCA as follows:

Phone: 1800 931 678
Email: [info@afca.org.au](mailto:info@afca.org.au)
Website: [www.afca.org.au](http://www.afca.org.au/)
Post: GPO Box 3 Melbourne VIC 3001

AFCA services are provided to you free of charge. Your complaint must be referred to AFCA within 2 years of the complaint decision, unless AFCA considers special circumstances apply. If your complaint is not eligible for consideration by AFCA, you may have access to other external dispute resolution options.

**For policies purchased prior to 15 October 2026, please follow the below process:**

#### Step 1

Any enquiry or complaint relating to a Fast Cover travel insurance policy or claim should be addressed to us in the first instance. In most cases, we will be able to resolve Your concerns.

Fast Cover Travel Insurance

Email: info@fastcover.com.au

Phone: 1300 409 322

Mail: PO Box R1384, Royal Exchange NSW 1225

We will acknowledge receipt of your complaint within 1 business day and do our utmost to resolve the complaint to your satisfaction within 10 business days.

#### Step 2

If we cannot resolve your complaint to your satisfaction, we will escalate your matter to Lloyd’s Australia who will determine whether it will be reviewed by their office or the Lloyd’s UK Complaints team.

Lloyd’s contact details are:

Lloyd’s Australia Limited Email: idraustralia@lloyds.com

Phone: (02) 8298 0783

Post: *Level 32, 225 George Street, Sydney NSW 2000, Australia*

A final decision will be provided to you within 30 calendar days of the date on which you first made the complaint unless certain exceptions apply.

#### Step 3

You may refer your complaint to the Australian Financial Complaints Authority (AFCA), if your complaint is not resolved to your satisfaction within 30 calendar days of the date on which you first made the complaint or at any time.

AFCA can be contacted as follows:

Phone: 1800 931 678

Email: info@afca.org.au

Website: www.afca.org.au

Post: GPO Box 3 Melbourne VIC 3001

Your complaint must be referred to AFCA within 2 years of the final decision, unless AFCA considers special circumstances apply.

If your complaint is not eligible for consideration by AFCA, you may be referred to the Financial Ombudsman Service (UK) or you can seek independent legal advice. You can also access any other external dispute resolution or other options that may be available to you.

### How long does it take to get ETIAS from Australia?

### How is Depreciation applied to items under my travel insurance policy?

Depreciation is applied to Unspecified luggage and personal effects based on the age of the item and its expected wear and tear over time. The amount claimable is limited to the original purchase price of the item, less any applicable depreciation, and subject to the benefit limits and sub-limits outlined in the Product Disclosure Statement (PDS).

Depreciation is not applied to:

- Luggage and personal effects purchased duty-free prior to departure
- Items purchased during your trip
- Specified High Value Items listed on your Certificate of Insurance

Depreciation for Unspecified items is applied monthly from the date of purchase, up to a maximum percentage of the original purchase cost. Depreciation will be applied to claims for Unspecified luggage and personal effects and relevant items as follows:

| |
| --- |
| **Depreciation Table for Unspecified Luggage and Personal Effects** |
| **Luggage or Personal Effects Item Claimed** | **Types of items** *(but not limited to the below examples)* | **Depreciation amount applied from the date of purchase.** *(Applied for each month **you** have owned the item)* | **Maximum depreciation applicable** *(% of original purchase cost)* |
| **Toiletries** | Cosmetics, moisturiser, skin care, make-up, perfume, hair products and medications | 3% per month | Maximum of 80% |
| **Computers and Electrical Devices** | Personal Computers, video recorders, cameras, photographic equipment, mobile phones, tablets, personal computers, and electronics devices or equipment | 1.75% per month | Maximum of 60% |
| **Clothing, Shoes, Luggage and Books** | Your clothing (including sporting clothing), shoes, suitcase, handbags, jackets, underwear, accessories (*but not jewellery*), Prescription eye glasses and sun glasses. | 1.75% per month | Maximum of 80% |
| **Camping, Sporting and Snow Sports equipment, musical and leisure equipment** (but not clothing) | Skis, snowboards, guitars, bicycles, tennis racket, golf clubs | 1% per month | Maximum of 60% |
| **Jewellery** | Earrings, Ring, Necklace, Bracelet | 0.25% per month | Maximum of 25% |
| **All other items** | | 1.25% per month | Maximum of 60% |

Eligibility criteria, policy terms, conditions, exclusions, limits and sub limits apply. Consider the PDS prior to deciding on which policy is right for you and your needs.

### How many people can I include in my travel insurance policy?

Fast Cover offers different cover types depending on who you’re travelling with:

**Single policy** – Covers you and your dependants (your children or grandchildren under 21 who are not in full-time employment) travelling with you.

**Duo policy** – Covers two travellers on the same policy. The travellers don’t need to be related.

**Family policy** – Covers you, plus one of the following:

- You and your spouse (or partner) and your dependants, or
- You and your spouse (or partner) and your grandchildren, or
- You and your son or daughter and your grandchildren.

Every claim is reviewed individually on a case-by-case basis and will only be paid if it meets the terms, conditions, limits, and exclusions in your policy. Always check the PDS carefully so you know exactly what’s included before you travel.

### How much cover does the Bicycle Pack provide?

The Bicycle Pack is an optional add-on that provides protection if your bicycle is permanently lost, stolen, or accidentally damaged during your trip. The benefit limits are:

- Comprehensive (Single, Duo, Family): Up to $5,000 per bicycle, with a maximum of $15,000 for all claims combined
- Standard Saver (Single, Duo, Family): Up to $5,000 per bicycle, with a maximum of $15,000 for all claims combined
- Domestic Plus (Single, Duo, Family): Up to $5,000 per bicycle, with a maximum of $15,000 for all claims combined
- Frequent Traveller Saver: Up to $5,000 per bicycle, with a maximum of $15,000 for all claims combined
- Snow Sports Plus (Single, Duo, Family): Up to $5,000 per bicycle, with a maximum of $15,000 for all claims combined

The Bicycle Pack is not available with the Basics policy.

Eligibility requirements apply, including (but not limited to these) that the bicycle must be less than 3 years old, have a value of at least $1,500, and be free of defects when cover starts. Cover does not apply while the bicycle is being used.

Every claim is reviewed individually on a case-by-case basis and will only be paid if it meets the terms, conditions, limits, and exclusions in your policy. Always check the PDS carefully so you know exactly what’s included before you travel.

### How much cover is available for Travel Delay Expenses?

Travel Delay Expenses cover reasonable extra costs you might face if your pre-booked transport is unexpectedly cancelled, rescheduled or delayed. The amount you’re covered for depends on your policy type. The maximum limit is capped at $2,000; the travel delay benefit works to reimburse you $200 for reasonable additional meals and accommodation if your pre-booked carrier has been cancelled and rescheduled or delayed and the rescheduled departure time or delay is for at least 6 hours. Then for each subsequent full 24-hour period beyond the initial 6-hour delay, you receive another $200 up to the maximum of $2,000.

Your Certificate of Insurance will show the exact limits that apply to your policy.

Every claim is reviewed individually on a case-by-case basis and will only be paid if it meets the terms, conditions, limits, and exclusions in your policy. Always check the PDS carefully so you know exactly what’s included before you travel.

### How much does Comprehensive travel insurance cost?

- The excess you choose

- When you purchase the policy in relation to your departure date

### How much can I claim if my trip is disrupted and I have to return home?

If your trip is unexpectedly disrupted for a covered reason, the maximum you can claim is:

- Up to $50,000 under Comprehensive, Snow Sports Plus, Domestic Plus, and Frequent Traveller policies
- Up to $30,000 under Standard Saver policies

Every claim is reviewed individually on a case-by-case basis and will only be paid if it meets the terms, conditions, limits, and exclusions in your policy. Always check the PDS carefully so you know exactly what’s included before you travel.

### How will I receive my travel insurance claim number?

Once you lodge a claim with Fast Cover, a claim number will be issued to you. This number is a unique identifier for your claim and is different from your policy number.

The way you receive your claim number depends on how your claim is submitted:

- Online Claim: If you submit your claim online via the Fast Cover website, your claim number will be generated and provided immediately after submission.
- Email or Post: If you submit your claim by email or post, the Claims Team will issue your claim number within 10 business days of receiving your claim.
- Phone Claim: If you lodge your claim over the phone, the Claims Team will advise you of your claim number during the call.

If you have not received a claim number but have submitted your documentation, you should use your policy number in all communications with the Claims Team until your claim number is confirmed.

Claims can be submitted in writing, and Fast Cover aims to process claims within 10 business days of receiving a completed claim form and all necessary supporting documentation. If further information is required, you will be notified in writing within 10 business days.

For assistance or to follow up on your claim, you can contact the Claims Team on:

- 1300 409 322 (option 3) if calling within Australia
- +61 2 8215 7239 if calling from overseas
- You can also visit [fastcover.com.au/claims](https://www.fastcover.com.au/claims) for more information.

Eligibility criteria, policy terms, conditions, exclusions, limits and sub limits apply. Consider the PDS prior to deciding on which policy is right for you and your needs.

Any advice is general advice only and does not take into account your individual objectives, financial situation, or needs. Please consider the PDS before making any decisions regarding the purchase of travel insurance.

As each individual’s circumstances are different, we will assess each claim on a case-by-case basis in accordance with your specific circumstances, policy terms, and Certificate of Insurance.

### How should I enter my return date when purchasing a travel insurance policy?

Your return date must be the date you physically arrive back in Australia, not the date you board your return flight overseas. If you list your return date as the day you board your return flight overseas rather than the actual arrival date in Australia, you will not be covered for any events that occur after the stated return date.

### How to buy Family travel insurance at Fast Cover

### I have a local motorcycle licence, but not an Australian motorcycle licence - am I covered?

You are NOT automatically covered to ride a motorcycle, moped or scooter. For cover to be available to ride a motorcycle, moped or scooter you need to:

1. Take out the Motorcycle Pack and pay the additional premium
2. Comply with the requirements as per stated in our PDS regarding riding or being a passenger on a motorcycle, moped or scooter.

We note the following licencing requirements:

- if you are the rider in control of the motorcycle, moped or scooter with an engine capacity of 125cc or less, you need to hold both a current Australian Drivers License (Provisional or higher) (regardless of the local laws) and a licence valid for the country that you are riding in.
- if you are the rider in control of the motorcycle, moped or scooter with an engine capacity of with an engine capacity greater than 125cc, you must hold both a current Australian Motorcycle Licence (Provisional or higher) valid for the same class of motorcycle, moped or scooter (regardless of the local laws) and a licence valid for the country that you are riding in.

As each individual’s circumstances are different, we will assess each claim on a case by case basis and in accordance with your specific circumstances, policy terms and Certificate of Insurance.

### I have a visa exemption for the Schengen Area, do I still need to apply for an ETIAS?

Once the [ETIAS](https://home-affairs.ec.europa.eu/policies/schengen/smart-borders/european-travel-information-authorisation-system_en) becomes operational in late 2026, all visa-exempt nationals including Australians will need to obtain an ETIAS authorisation before travelling to the Schengen Area.

The ETIAS is not replacing the visa exemption but adding a pre-travel screening layer. You will still benefit from visa-free travel, but will need to complete the ETIAS registration online before your trip. The ETIAS authorisation may be valid for multiple entries over three years or until your passport expires, whichever comes first. The application process may be simpler than a visa application, entirely online, and with a lower fee (approximately AUD $11 or free for those under 18 or over 70).

As entry and visa requirements for Europe and the Schengen Area may change over time, it is your responsibility to verify entry and visa requirements with the official government authorities including the [European Commission](https://home-affairs.ec.europa.eu/policies/schengen/visa-policy) and the embassy or consulate of the European country you plan to visit.

*Source: <https://fastcover.com.au/faq/i-have-a-visa-exemption-for-the-schengen-area-do-i-still-need-to-apply-for-an-etias>*

- You have taken out a Snow Sports Plus policy or Domestic Plus policy
- You are 69 years of age or younger at the date of policy issue if you take out a Snow Sports Plus policy
- You only participate in backcountry skiing or snowboarding with a professional snow sports instructor as defined under our PDS

For more information about terms and conditions of cover for backcountry skiing, read our PDS to understand what is covered and what is not covered.

### I’m a temporary resident of Australia — can I buy travel insurance if my health insurance ends when I leave for my holiday?

Unfortunately, you won’t be eligible for a Fast Cover travel insurance policy if your Australian private health insurance ends before your return to Australia.

To be eligible, your private health insurance must remain valid for the entire duration of your trip and still be active when you return to Australia. This requirement ensures that if you are seriously injured overseas and need to be repatriated for treatment, you are covered when you arrive back in Australia.

#### To be eligible for a policy as a temporary resident of Australia, you must meet all of the following conditions:

- you are a non-permanent resident who holds a valid Medicare card or are covered by an Australian private health insurance policy that satisfies the government health insurance requirements for your visa type and remains valid beyond the period of your policy; and
- your visa remains valid beyond the period of your return; and
- you have a home in Australia to which you intend to return; and
- your trip starts and ends in Australia; and
- you hold a return ticket to Australia; and
- you meet any other eligibility criteria we apply in the application process.

Every claim is reviewed individually on a case-by-case basis and will only be paid if it meets the terms, conditions, limits, and exclusions in your policy. Always check the PDS carefully so you know exactly what’s included before you travel.

### I’m an Australian resident living overseas, can I buy a policy to cover travel back to Australia?

Fast Cover policies don’t cover trips that start overseas and end in Australia, even if you’re an Australian resident. Our policies are designed for travellers who depart from Australia and return to Australia at the end of their trip.

However, you may be eligible to purchase a policy while already overseas if you meet all of the requirements for this cover type. This policy is designed for travellers who are already outside Australia and need travel insurance for the remainder of their trip.

Every claim is reviewed individually on a case-by-case basis and will only be paid if it meets the terms, conditions, limits, and exclusions in your policy. Always check the PDS carefully so you know exactly what’s included before you travel.

### I am not happy with my claim outcome, what do I need to do?

If you’re not satisfied with the outcome of your claim, we’ll do our best to work with you to resolve the issue. There is a formal process you can follow:

**For policies purchased on or after 15 October 2026, please follow the below process:**

**Step 1**

Please contact:

Fast Cover Travel Insurance
Email: [info@fastcover.com.au](mailto:info@fastcover.com.au)
Phone: [1300 409 322](tel:1300409322)
Mail: PO Box R1384, Royal Exchange NSW 1225

We will acknowledge receipt of your complaint and we will aim to resolve the complaint to your satisfaction.

A complaint decision will be provided to you within 30 calendar days. If we are unable to meet this timeframe we will inform you of the reason for the delay.

**Step 2**

If your complaint is not resolved to your satisfaction, or you do not receive a complaint decision within 30 calendar days of the date on which you first made the complaint, you can refer your complaint to the Australian Financial Complaints Authority (AFCA). You can contact AFCA as follows:

Phone: 1800 931 678
Email: [info@afca.org.au](mailto:info@afca.org.au)
Website: [www.afca.org.au](http://www.afca.org.au/)
Post: GPO Box 3 Melbourne VIC 3001

AFCA services are provided to you free of charge. Your complaint must be referred to AFCA within 2 years of the complaint decision, unless AFCA considers special circumstances apply. If your complaint is not eligible for consideration by AFCA, you may have access to other external dispute resolution options.

**For policies purchased prior to 15 October 2026, please follow the below process:**

**Stage 1:** **Contact us**

Inform us of your complaint via phone, email or post. We will acknowledge when we receive your complaint and do our best to resolve it to your satisfaction within 10 business days. If we cannot resolve your complaint within 10 business days, we will provide you with an update every 10 business days, unless you agree to a different timeframe.

Fast Cover Travel Insurance

Phone: 1300 409 322

Email: [info@fastcover.com.au](mailto:info@fastcover.com.au)

Post: PO Box R1384, Royal Exchange NSW 1225

**Stage 2:** **Complaint Review**

If we cannot resolve your complaint to your satisfaction, we will escalate your complaint to Lloyds Australia. A final decision will be provided to you within 30 days of the date you first made the complaint. If a decision cannot be made within this timeframe, you will be contacted in writing before the deadline with the reason for the delay. You will also be informed of your right to take your complaint to the Australian Financial Complaints Authority (AFCA) and how to do so.

Lloyd’s Australia Limited

Phone: 02 8298 0783

Email: [idraustralia@lloyds.com](mailto:idraustralia@lloyds.com)

Post: PO Box R1745, Royal Exchange NSW 1225

**Stage 3: External review**

If you’re still unhappy with our decision, or if we haven’t responded within 30 days, you can escalate your complaint to the Australian Financial Complaints Authority (AFCA). This is a free and independent service:

- Website: [www.afca.org.au](https://www.afca.org.au/)
- Email: [info@afca.org.au](mailto:info@afca.org.au)
- Phone: 1800 931 678

AFCA’s decision is binding on us, but not on you. You also retain the right to seek legal assistance if you wish.

*Source: <https://fastcover.com.au/faq/i-am-not-happy-with-my-claim-outcome-what-do-i-need-to-do>*

### I am travelling overseas and then around Australia, what am I covered for while in Australia?

If you have an international policy and travel around Australia as a part of your trip, the domestic portion of your trip will only be covered by policy benefits that apply to domestic travel. This means that you will have cover as per the benefits on your international policy, excluding the following benefits (even if they are included in your overseas policy) while you are travelling domestically:

- Overseas 24/7 Emergency Medical Assistance
- Overseas Emergency Medical and Hospital Expenses
- Overseas Emergency Dental
- Overseas Emergency Evacuation and Repatriation
- Overseas Hospital Cash Payment
- Permanent Disability
- Loss of Income
- Passport, Credit Cards & Credit Card Fraud
- Theft of Cash
- Delay of Luggage and Personal Effects
- Motorcycle Pack
- Covid-19 Overseas Emergency Medical, Hospital and Medical Evacuation Expenses

**However, if you are travelling on a cruise within Australia, you might get some other benefits like 24/7 Emergency Assistance, Emergency Overseas Medical, Emergency Medical Evacuation. Please call our friendly team for exploring the right travel insurance product.**

As each individual’s circumstances are different, we will assess each claim on a case-by-case basis and in accordance with your specific circumstances, policy terms and Certificate of Insurance.

Any advice is general advice only and does not take into account your individual objectives, financial situation or needs. Consider the PDS as eligibility criteria, policy terms, conditions, exclusions and limits apply.

### I’m only in transit in Bali. Do I still need travel insurance for Bali?

### I have a heart condition but full medical cover through work. Can I still buy travel insurance for cancellation and other benefits?

You can still buy a Fast Cover travel insurance policy if you want cover for Trip Cancellation, Luggage, Trip Disruption, and other non-medical benefits available, even if you already have full medical cover through your work.

If you choose not to complete a medical screening for your heart condition, you won’t be covered for any claims related to that condition. This includes Trip Cancellations, Trip Disruptions, or Overseas Emergency Medical and Hospital Expenses that arise from your heart condition. However, you may still have cover for other policy benefits that are not connected to your condition, depending on the policy you select.

It’s important to note that the Overseas Emergency Medical and Hospital Expenses benefit is included in all international travel insurance policies (Comprehensive, Standard Saver, Basics, Snow Sports Plus, and Frequent Traveller Saver). But it will not apply to claims connected to undeclared or excluded pre-existing conditions such as a heart condition.

Every claim is reviewed individually on a case-by-case basis and will only be paid if it meets the terms, conditions, limits, and exclusions in your policy. Always check the PDS carefully so you know exactly what’s included before you travel.

As entry and visa requirements for the US may change over time, it is your responsibility to verify entry and visa requirements with the official government authorities including the [US Department of State - Bureau of Consular Affairs](https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/us-visas.html), the [United States Customs and Border Protection](https://www.cbp.gov/) (CBP), the [US Embassy in Australia](https://au.usembassy.gov/visas/) or your local US Consulate.

### I have a policy without snow sports cover, but can I be covered for snow sports for just a part of my trip?

To have cover for snow sports, you have two options:

1) You can upgrade your whole policy to a Snow Sports Plus policy and pay the additional premium, or

2) You can purchase a separate Snow Sports Plus already overseas policy just for the period that you will be doing snow sports. In this option, you will have two policies (your normal policy covering the whole time that you are overseas for, and the shorter Snow Sports Plus Already Overseas policy only covering the time that you will be doing snow sports) running in parallel for the period of time that you have the Snow Sports Plus policy.

It's important to know that an Already Overseas policy comes with a $500 excess, a 48-hour waiting period before cover starts, and an age limit of 65 years. In addition to that, the Already Overseas Snow Sports Plus policy can only be issued for up to 21 days.

Cover is subject to the policy terms, conditions, limits and exclusions in the Product Disclosure Statement (PDS).

*Source: <https://fastcover.com.au/faq/i-have-a-policy-without-snow-sports-cover-but-can-i-be-covered-for-snow-sports-for-just-a-part-of-my-trip>*

### I’m a business traveller - how does GST affect my claim?

If you are travelling for business and are entitled to claim an input tax credit (ITC) for expenses you’ve claimed on your travel insurance, the amount we pay will be reduced by the value of that input tax credit. This also applies if you would be entitled to an ITC when replacing an item (for example, if luggage was lost or stolen).

For travel within Australia only, if you are entitled to an ITC on your premium, you must tell us the percentage of that credit at the time you first make a claim. If you don’t provide this information, you may have a liability for GST if we pay you under this policy.

This ensures that claims are settled fairly and in line with tax rules that apply to business travellers.

*Source: <https://fastcover.com.au/faq/i-m-a-business-traveller-how-does-gst-affect-my-claim>*

### I need to cancel my policy because of the Coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. What are my options?

If you no longer wish to travel due to the COVID-19 pandemic and need to cancel your travel insurance policy, your options will depend on when you purchased the policy and whether your trip has started.

- If you are within the 25-day cooling-off period and your trip has not yet begun, you can generally cancel your policy and receive a full refund of your premium.
- If the cooling-off period has passed, but your trip has not yet started, you may still be able to make changes to the departure and return dates of your policy if your travel plans are postponed. Any premium differences will be adjusted depending on your new trip details.
- If your trip has already commenced or if you have made a claim or intend to make a claim or have exercised any of your rights under policy such as using your travel insurance policy to obtain a visa or enter into a country, the policy cannot be cancelled for a refund.

It’s important to note that travel insurance does not provide cover for every COVID-19 situation, and there is no cover for cancellation simply because of general concerns about the pandemic or government travel restrictions.

Every request and claim is reviewed individually on a case-by-case basis and will only be approved if it meets the terms, conditions, limits, and exclusions in your policy. Always check the PDS carefully so you know exactly what’s included before making any decisions.

*Source: <https://fastcover.com.au/faq/i-need-to-cancel-my-policy-because-of-the-coronavirus-covid-19-pandemic-what-are-my-options>*

### If I hike up to altitudes over 6,000m, but have an accident below 6,000m, am I covered?

There is NO cover for hiking over 6000m, even if you have taken out the [**Adventure Pack**](../adventure-travel-insurance).

You are automatically covered to hike up to 3000m only. To be covered to hike up to 6000m, you will need to take out the Adventure pack and pay the additional premium.

Whether or not you are covered for your accident depends on the altitude where the accident occurred:

- **Accident occurred at an altitude over 6000m:** If you have the Adventure Pack and the accident occurs at an altitude of over 6000m, this would not be covered as the accident occurred when you were at an altitude of over 6000m.
- **Accident occurred at an altitude under 6000m and over 3000m:** If you have the Adventure Pack, you would have provision to claim. If you do not have the Adventure Pack, you would not have provision to claim.
- **Accident occurred at an altitude under 3000m:** You would have provision to claim if you have an accident.

Cover is subject to the policy terms, conditions, limits and exclusions in the [**Product Disclosure Statement (PDS)**](../pds).

*Source: <https://fastcover.com.au/faq/if-i-hike-up-to-altitudes-over-6-000m-but-have-an-accident-below-6-000m-am-i-covered>*

### If I have Car Hire Excess Cover, do I still need to take the insurance offered by the rental company?

The insurance offered by your car rental company is not replaced by rental car excess cover, as rental car excess insurance only covers the EXCESS component of that rental car insurance. You will still need to take out regular rental car insurance with the rental car company.

If you do not have rental vehicle insurance for your rental car and it is damaged or stolen, you will be liable for the repair or replacement costs. In order for you to claim for car hire excess cover, you must have rental car insurance and also purchased the car hire excess cover on your travel insurance policy.

For more information, refer to our [Product Disclosure Statement (PDS)](https://fastcover.com.au/pds).

### If I need a green card can I purchase a policy?

If you are a temporary resident of Australia, you would be eligible to purchase a policy with us, only if:

- You are a non-permanent resident who holds a valid Medicare card or are covered by an Australian Private Health Insurance policy that satisfies the government health insurance requirements for your visa type; and
- You have a home in Australia to which you intend to return; and
- Your trip starts and ends in Australia; and
- You hold a return ticket to Australia; and
- You are aged 89 years and under.

#### Note:

- In the event of a medical repatriation from overseas, we will return you to Australia.
- Medical expenses incurred once you have returned to Australia are not covered on this policy.
- It is therefore important that you ensure you have access to long term medical care in Australia.

If you do not satisfy the above conditions, you cannot buy a Travel Insurance policy. If you do, it will be INVALID. You can contact [The Insurance Council of Australia](https://insurancecouncil.com.au/), who may be able to give you a list of travel insurers who may be able to provide you with cover.

Cover is subject to the policy terms, conditions, limits and exclusions in the [Product Disclosure Statement (PDS)](https://fastcover.com.au/pds).

### If I return home temporarily during my trip, will my overseas cover be suspended?

Yes. If you return home early for any reason, your cover will be suspended from the time you arrive back in Australia until you leave again to continue your trip. To resume cover, you must have at least 14 days remaining on your policy as shown on your Certificate of Insurance.

Once you restart your trip, your policy will continue until the end date on your Certificate of Insurance, or until you permanently return home, whichever comes first. Please note that the policy will not cover the costs of returning to Australia unless those costs are covered by the policy.

Every claim is reviewed individually on a case-by-case basis and will only be paid if it meets the terms, conditions, limits, and exclusions in your policy. Always check the PDS carefully so you know exactly what’s included before you travel.

### I still plan to travel during the Coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. Will I have cover?

You can still buy and use travel insurance if you are travelling during the **C**OVID-19 pandemic, but it’s important to understand what is and isn’t covered. Depending on the policy you purchase, you may have cover for:

- COVID-19 overseas emergency medical and hospital expenses if you are diagnosed with COVID-19 by a medical practitioner following a PCR test while overseas.
- COVID-19 medical evacuation and repatriation if medically necessary and approved.
- COVID-19 Trip disruption expenses if you or someone insured on your Certificate of Insurance tests positive to COVID-19 and are required to quarantine overseas.

There is **no cover** for some situations, such as government-imposed border closures, quarantine requirements that are not linked to a covered diagnosis or being denied boarding due to vaccination requirements.

### If my phone breaks while overseas, am I covered to have it repaired or replaced?

Depending on the policy you have chosen, cover may be available under the Luggage and Personal Effects benefit of your Fast Cover Travel Insurance policy if your phone is damaged while overseas. Cover is available under the policy benefit, for the damage, loss or theft of your phone, which can include the cost of phone repair or replacement, up to a maximum sub-limit of $1,500 per unspecified item (which includes mobile phones). Other maximum benefit limits also apply, depending on the policy chosen. Coverage is subject to the terms, conditions, exclusions, limits and sub-limits outlined in the Product Disclosure Statement (PDS).

The amount payable will be the cost of repair, replacement or the purchase price of the phone minus any applicable depreciation, whichever is lesser, applied as outlined in the Product Disclosure Statement.

To make a claim for phone repair or replacement:

- Ensure you have proof of ownership of the phone
- Obtain and keep all receipts and documents related to the repair or replacement
- If a claim relates to a mobile phone or device with phone capabilities, You must supply Us the IMEI (International Mobile Equipment Identity) number. You must also block the IMEI number with Your telecommunications provider
- If required, provide a repair report displaying the cost of the repair amount, charged by the repairer (please note, the cost to obtain this report is not covered)
- Submit your claim for assessment through the Fast Cover claims process.

It is important to be aware of important cover conditions, as well as exclusions that may apply, including but not limited to:

- The damage arises from an electrical or mechanical breakdown
- The damage arises from ordinary wear and tear, deterioration, atmospheric or weather conditions, insects, rodents, or vermin
- There is no cover if damage is to items that do not belong to you

Eligibility criteria, policy terms, conditions, exclusions, limits and sub limits apply. Consider the PDS prior to deciding on which policy is right for you and your needs.

Any advice is general advice only and does not take into account your individual objectives, financial situation, or needs. Please consider the PDS before making any decisions regarding the purchase of travel insurance.

As each individual’s circumstances are different, we will assess each claim on a case-by-case basis in accordance with your specific circumstances, policy terms, and Certificate of Insurance

### I’ve received a quote but can’t see the excess, how do I check, and what options are available?

The excess on your travel insurance depends on when the policy was purchased and the option you selected during the quote.

If you buy your policy before leaving Australia, you can usually choose from $500, $200, or $100 excess options. A lower excess generally means a higher premium. The selected excess applies to most claims, although some sections of the policy may have different rules.

If you purchase a policy while already overseas, the excess is fixed at $500 and cannot be changed.

To check your chosen excess, review your quote summary or your Certificate of Insurance (if you’ve already purchased). You can also log into your policy online or contact us at [info@fastcover.com.au](mailto:info@fastcover.com.au) or 1300 409 322 for help.

### If I am denied entry to a country because I didn't get vaccinated, can I claim for cancellation?

If you are denied entry to a country because you did not get the required vaccination and you do not have a valid reason for not getting the vaccine, your claim may be denied. The Claims Team will assess each claim on a case by case basis.

> For example: A valid reason could be due to a medical condition that we are able to cover you for, or if you are pregnant.

If the reason you are denied entry to a country is due to you acting illegally or breaking any government prohibition, laws or regulation including visa requirements, your claim may be denied. This is a General Exclusion in our [Product Disclosure Statement (PDS)](https://fastcover.com.au/pds).

For more information, check out the [Smartraveller health page](http://smartraveller.gov.au/guide/all-travellers/health/Pages/health-checks-and-vaccinations.aspx).

#### COVID-19 Vaccinations

There is no cover if your claim arises:

- from you acting unlawfully or breaking any government prohibition, laws or regulation including visa requirements (such as COVID-19 vaccination requirements).
- from the denial of boarding of any airline, shipping line or other carrier due to COVID-19 vaccination requirements.

Cover is subject to the policy terms, conditions, limits and exclusions in the [Product Disclosure Statement (PDS)](https://fastcover.com.au/pds).

### If the airline gives me a full credit for my airfares, but my new fares are more expensive, can I claim for the extra cost?

### If I am overseas and I claim for cancellation expenses for a trip which is within my travel dates, does my policy end?

#### If you are already travelling:

If your trip is unexpectedly disrupted and it is for reasons that you can claim for, you can submit a claim for trip disruption expenses and your policy will not end.

#### If you have not yet left for your trip:

If you have to [unexpectedly cancel your trip](https://fastcover.com.au/travel-insurance/cancellation-benefits) for a reason that you can claim for, and you submit a cancellation claim, your policy will end. Another travel insurance policy will need to be purchased for a new trip.

Cover is subject to the policy terms, conditions, limits and exclusions in the [Product Disclosure Statement (PDS)](https://fastcover.com.au/pds).

### If we are unsure whether we are going skiing, can we upgrade to a ski policy later?

Yes, you may be able to upgrade to a Snow Sports Plus policy while you are already overseas by paying the difference in premium.

Another option is to purchase a separate Snow Sports Plus Already Overseas policy just for the time you’ll be skiing or snowboarding. In this case, you’ll hold two policies: your original one covering your whole trip, and the shorter Snow Sports Plus Already Overseas policy running in parallel for the snow sports portion.

Keep in mind that Already Overseas policies have some key differences: they come with a $500 excess, a 48-hour waiting period before cover begins, an age limit of 65 years, and a maximum duration of 21 days.

All cover is subject to the terms, conditions, limits and exclusions in the Product Disclosure Statement (PDS).

*Source: <https://fastcover.com.au/faq/if-we-are-unsure-whether-we-are-going-skiing-can-we-upgrade-to-a-ski-policy-later>*

### If we’re on a Duo policy and both of our luggage is stolen, is it treated as one claim or two?

A Duo policy covers two travellers under the same policy, but when it comes to claims, what matters is whether the loss comes from one event or separate events. Only one excess applies when multiple claims arise from the same event, but if the losses come from separate, unrelated events, an excess applies to each claim.

So if both of your bags are stolen at the same time in the same incident, it’s considered one event. If your bags are stolen at different times or in different situations, those are treated as separate events.

Every claim is reviewed individually on a case-by-case basis and will only be paid if it meets the terms, conditions, limits, and exclusions in your policy. Always check the PDS carefully so you know exactly what’s included before you travel.

### If I die before my trip starts, is the Accidental Death benefit payable?

No, the Accidental Death benefit only applies if you die as the direct result of an injury that occurs during your trip. If you pass away before your journey begins, this benefit is not payable.

Every claim is reviewed individually on a case-by-case basis and will only be paid if it meets the terms, conditions, limits, and exclusions in your policy. Always check the PDS carefully so you know exactly what’s included before you travel.

*Source: <https://fastcover.com.au/faq/if-i-die-before-my-trip-starts-is-the-accidental-death-benefit-payable>*

### I'm going skiing for a day. Am I covered if I injure myself while skiing overseas if I don't have Snow Sports cover?

No, there is no cover for overseas emergency medical and hospital expenses if you do not have a Snow Sports Plus policy and you become injured whilst participating in any snow sports listed in our PDS. You must take out a Snow Sports Plus policy if you would like to be covered for participation in any snow sports listed in our PDS.

Read our PDS to learn more about conditions of cover for Snow Sports and what is included.

### I’m only in transit in Asia. Do I still need travel insurance for Asia?

### I'm hiring my campervan from Camplify, am I eligible for the Rental Vehicle Excess cover?

Rental vehicle insurance excess cover extends to campervans that do not exceed 4.5 tonnes, rented from a licensed motor vehicle rental company including peer-to-peer carsharing platforms.

Eligibility criteria, policy terms, conditions, exclusions and limits apply. Consider the PDS prior to deciding on which policy is right for you and your needs.

As each individual’s circumstances are different, we will assess each claim on a case by case basis and in accordance with your specific circumstances, policy terms and Certificate of Insurance.

### If I’ve already spoken to the Emergency Assistance team, do I still need to submit a claim form?

Yes, even if the Emergency Assistance team has been in touch about your incident, you’ll still need to complete a claim form. This is because the Claims team requires documentation to properly assess your claim.

- **If you already have a Claim Number:** Include it on your claim form.
- **If you don’t have a Claim Number yet:** Use your policy number instead, and the Claims team will issue you one once they receive your claim.

Every claim is reviewed individually on a case-by-case basis and will only be paid if it meets the terms, conditions, limits, and exclusions in your policy. Always check the PDS carefully so you know exactly what’s included before you travel.

*Source: <https://fastcover.com.au/faq/if-i-ve-already-spoken-to-the-emergency-assistance-team-do-i-still-need-to-submit-a-claim-form>*

### I'm just walking in the snow, and not doing any snow sports. Do I need a Snow Sports policy?

If you will not be participating in any snow sports, for example, not participating in snowshoeing or any other snow sports activity, you do not need to purchase a Snow Sports Plus policy.

Under our PDS snowshoeing is listed as a snow sport. While snowshoeing is not specifically defined in our PDS, it generally describes an activity where people walk on snow using snowshoes to prevent sinking into the snow. You may wish to consider if you will be participating in snowshoeing as it is listed as a snow sport under our PDS. To have cover for snowshoeing you would require the Snow Sports Plus policy.

Read our PDS to learn more about conditions of cover for Snow Sports and what is included.

### I'm doing backcountry skiing with a professional guide, but not a professional snow sports instructor. Am I covered?

Cover may be available for backcountry skiing with a professional snow sports instructor provided:

- You have taken out a Snow Sports Plus policy or Domestic Plus policy
- You are 69 years of age or younger at the date of policy issue if you take out a Snow Sport Plus Policy
- You only participate in backcountry skiing with a professional snow sport instructor as defined under our PDS

A professional snow sports instructor is defined under our PDS as the holder of an Alpine Level 4 certification recognised by the International Ski Instructors Association (ISIA) or the holder of a Canada Ski Guide (CSGI) Level 3 Certification (or ISIA recognised equivalent). Such guides have a minimum of 2 years’ experience as a trainee guide and have completed the required training to lead groups in Backcountry areas without supervision. They have been trained in all aspects of Backcountry and avalanche safety and are familiar with the areas they are guiding and instructing in. They hold the required insurances and permits to guide groups in Backcountry areas on a commercial basis.

For more information about terms and conditions of cover for backcountry skiing and snowboarding, read our PDS to understand what is covered and what is not covered

*Source: <https://fastcover.com.au/faq/im-doing-backcountry-skiing-with-a-professional-guide-but-not-a-professional-snow-sports-instructor-am-i-covered>*

### Is a 75th birthday party considered a 'Special Event'?

Eligibility criteria, policy terms, conditions, exclusions and limits apply. Consider the PDS prior to deciding on which policy is right for you and your needs.

### Is a multi-trip travel insurance policy available for seniors?

Multi-trip cover is offered through the Frequent Traveller Saver policy. This type of policy is available to travellers up to the age of 75. It allows multiple trips within a 12-month period, with each trip limited to the maximum duration selected when purchasing the policy, such as 15, 25, 40, or 63 days or less.

Travellers over 75 are not eligible for a Frequent Traveller Saver policy but may still be able to take out a Single Trip policy, depending on age limits and the destinations chosen. It is important to review the Product Disclosure Statement (PDS) to confirm the eligibility rules for each policy type.

### Is 80 Too Old to Travel?

Seniors in their 80s can enjoy rewarding travel experiences with thoughtful planning. Opt for destinations with accessible healthcare facilities and accommodation. Stay hydrated, pack necessary medications in your carry-on, and limit strenuous activities. Booking direct flights and using airport airline assistance for seniors minimises stress and ensures you are taking measures towards a hassle-free trip.

Fast Cover offers seniors travel insurance for 80 year olds (up to age 89 at the time of policy issue). Eligibility criteria, policy terms, conditions, exclusions, and limits apply. Consider the PDS before deciding on which policy is right for you and your needs.

### Is cruise cover automatically included with my policy?

Only our Frequent Traveller Saver policies automatically include cover for cruising.

Note: It is not possible to remove cruise cover from your Frequent Traveller Saver policy.

If you are not taking out a Frequent Traveller Saver policy, you must answer 'Yes' when asked if you are going on a cruise when you get your quote, otherwise you will not have cover under any benefits for events related to your cruise.

Important note: You will not need to add ‘cruise cover’ to your policy if you are cruising within Australian waters, the New Zealand or the South Pacific Region for a day trip, within Asia, Europe or Worldwide Regions for less than 4 nights or travelling on a river cruise.

Eligibility criteria, policy terms, conditions, exclusions and limits apply. Consider the PDS prior to deciding on which policy is right for you and your needs.

*Source: <https://fastcover.com.au/faq/is-cruise-cover-automatically-included-with-my-policy>*

### Is an iPhone covered if it was a gift and is later lost or stolen?

Yes, the iPhone can be covered under **Benefit 14: Luggage and Personal Effects** up to a maximum of $1 500, if you have this cover under your policy.

If the item is lost, stolen or damaged, you would still need to prove ownership of the item. You can do this by requesting the receipt from the person who gifted you the iPhone, or by providing us with a photo of the item, along with the warranty card or user manual.

If you make a claim, we will fully assess your claim, as everyone's circumstances are different and we will assess each claim on a case by case basis.

Cover is subject to the policy terms, conditions, limits and exclusions in the [Product Disclosure Statement (PDS)](https://fastcover.com.au/pds).

### Is Diving underwater covered?

Diving underwater using an artificial breathing apparatus is included under Fast Cover travel insurance policies, provided the depth does not exceed 10 metres and you either hold an open water diving licence recognised in Australia or dive with an instructor licensed for these activities.

If you wish to dive between 10 and 30 metres, you must purchase the Adventure Pack add-on. The same licensing or supervision requirements apply. There is no cover for diving deeper than 30 metres.

If your trip includes one or more overnight stays in Australia, or four or more nights overseas on a cruise ship, you must also specify Cruise Cover for cover to apply.

Whether a claim for diving underwater is payable will depend on your policy type, the specific circumstances, the type of expenses you’re claiming, and the policy terms, conditions, exclusions, limits and sub-limits.

Every claim is reviewed individually on a case-by-case basis and will only be paid if it meets the terms, conditions, limits, and exclusions in your policy. Always check the PDS carefully so you know exactly what’s included before you travel.

*Source: <https://fastcover.com.au/faq/is-diving-underwater-covered>*

### Is a bicycle over 3 years old covered under travel insurance?

To be eligible for Bicycle Pack cover, your bicycle must be less than 3 years old, have a minimum value of $1,500, and be free of defects at the time cover starts. If your bicycle is more than 3 years old at the time of travel, it will not meet the eligibility criteria and cannot be covered under the Bicycle Pack.

Always review the Product Disclosure Statement (PDS) to confirm the full requirements, limits, and exclusions that apply to bicycle cover.

Every claim is reviewed individually on a case-by-case basis and will only be paid if it meets the terms, conditions, limits, and exclusions in your policy. Always check the PDS carefully so you know exactly what’s included before you travel.

### Is hiking, trekking or tramping covered under my travel insurance policy?

Hiking, trekking or tramping is included under Fast Cover travel insurance policies under specific conditions:

- These activities are automatically included within Covered Sports and Leisure Activities, peaking at altitudes below 3,000 metres, where specialist climbing equipment is not required. (Expeditions to or on the Kokoda Track/Trail are not automatically covered)
- If the activity is peaking at altitudes between 3,000 and 6,000 metres (not higher), you must purchase the Adventure Pack add-on. Even with the Adventure Pack, cover is only available if specialist climbing equipment is not required.
- There is no cover for hiking, trekking or tramping above 6,000 metres, or for any activity that involves the use of specialist climbing equipment.

Whether a claim relating to this activity is payable will depend on your policy type, the specific circumstances, the type of expenses you are seeking, and the policy terms, conditions, exclusions, limits and sub-limits.

Eligibility criteria, policy terms, conditions, exclusions, limits and sub-limits apply. Consider the PDS prior to deciding on which policy is right for you and your needs.

As each individual’s circumstances are different, we will assess each claim on a case-by-case basis in accordance with your specific circumstances, policy terms, conditions, exclusions and Certificate of Insurance.

### Is it worth it to get travel insurance?

The value of insurance may be considered to be worth it when you consider the cost of travel insurance cover, which is most likely to be relatively small compared to the cost of your total holiday. Costs may vary from a few hundred to hundreds of thousands for an unexpected overseas hospital visit depending on various factors. These costs can easily escalate with extended hospital stays and when a medivac is required to bring you back to Australia. We also provide 24-hour support from the [**Emergency Assistance**](../emergency-contacts) team if an emergency occurs.

For more information, refer to our Product Disclosure Statement (PDS) and TMD.
